Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.

 

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Senior HR Business Partner to support our Engineering and Product teams.

This is a role for someone who wants to be close to the business. You’ll work directly with leaders and managers on the people decisions that matter most as their teams grow: developing exceptional talent, building stronger managers, designing organizations, raising the performance bar and solving difficult people problems quickly.

You’ll also help build the systems behind that work. Mercor is still early, and many of the development programs and talent practices we need do not exist yet. We’re looking for someone who has built from 0 to 1 before and is excited to do it again.

What You’ll Do

  • Partner directly with Engineering and Product leaders on talent, organizational and people decisions.

  • Coach managers on performance, feedback, team effectiveness, development and difficult employee situations.

  • Identify what our highest-performing employees need to continue growing at Mercor and turn those needs into practical development opportunities.

  • Build development programs from 0 to 1, from identifying the problem through design, launch, adoption and iteration.

  • Partner with leaders on organizational design, role clarity, succession planning and talent movement as teams scale.

  • Run talent and performance processes for EPD while keeping the focus on judgment and outcomes rather than process for its own sake.

  • Spot patterns across teams and turn them into clear recommendations for leaders and the People team.

  • Work across Recruiting, People Operations and the broader People team to solve problems end to end.

  • Move quickly between strategic questions and hands-on execution. You should be equally comfortable advising a senior leader and building the first version of something yourself.

What We’re Looking For

  • 8+ years of strong HRBP experience: You have substantial experience partnering with Engineering, Product or similarly technical organizations and can build credibility with senior technical leaders.

  • Startup experience: You’ve worked in a fast-growing startup and understand the pace, ambiguity and changing needs that come with it.

  • 0→1 builder: You have personally built and launched development, talent or manager programs where little or no infrastructure existed before.

  • Excellent judgment: You can work through complex people situations, identify what actually matters and make clear recommendations without relying on a playbook for every answer.

  • Manager coach: You can make managers better, including experienced leaders who expect their HR partner to challenge their thinking.

  • High performance orientation: You know how to differentiate performance, develop exceptional people and address performance issues directly.

  • Operator mindset: You are comfortable creating the strategy and doing the work required to get it into practice.

  • Low-ego and direct: You communicate clearly, earn trust quickly and care more about getting to the right answer than owning the answer.

  • In-person: You are able to work from our San Francisco office five days a week.

Why Mercor

You’ll have the opportunity to shape how Engineering and Product teams develop as Mercor scales, while building many of the underlying People systems for the first time. This is a high-ownership role with direct access to leaders and the ability to see the impact of your work quickly.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

About the Role

As Senior Product Manager, Payments, you'll own how Mercor moves over $4 million a day to hundreds of thousands of experts in nearly every country on earth. Getting people paid accurately, quickly, and in the way they expect is the single most important promise we make to our workforce.

You'll own the payments platform end-to-end with significant autonomy, working directly with engineering, finance, and leadership to turn ambiguous problems into shipped products. You'll balance long-term platform strategy with rapid execution, making decisions that directly shape expert trust, operational cost, and the company's bottom line.

What You'll Do

  • Own the payout experience: Take full ownership of how experts get paid — from contract terms and time capture through disbursement, retries, and support resolution.

  • Build the ledger and money movement platform: Partner with engineering on the ledger, reconciliation, and payout automation that keep every dollar correct, traceable, and auditable at scale.

  • Expand global coverage: Grow the payout rails, methods, and currencies available to experts, weighing cost, speed, reliability, and local regulation market by market.

  • Understand the business: Work backwards from payout cost, failure rates, support volume, and expert retention to decide what gets built.

  • Get in the weeds: Write specs and PRDs, but also build the dashboards, dig through failed payouts, and make small PRs to unblock yourself.

  • Collaborate: Partner closely with engineering, finance, compliance, operations, and support to ship quickly without breaking trust.

What You'll Own

  • Payouts and disbursement: Global money movement to experts across rails, methods, and currencies.

  • Ledger and reconciliation: The canonical record of what is owed, paid, and settled.

  • Contracts, rates, and earnings: How work converts into money owed, and how experts see it.

  • Payments operations: The tooling that lets a small team run payouts at enormous scale.

What We're Looking For

  • Experience: 6+ years in product management, with meaningful time on payouts or disbursements specifically — not only payments acceptance or checkout. Prior SWE, ML, or DS experience preferred.

  • Payments depth: Working knowledge of payout rails, ledgers and double-entry accounting, reconciliation, FX, KYC, and tax and compliance requirements across markets.

  • High Ownership: You take full accountability for outcomes, not just outputs — including when money moves incorrectly.

  • Independence: Able to self-direct in ambiguous contexts, creating clarity for others.

  • Technical Fluency: Comfortable building scrappy MVPs, querying the data yourself, and reading enough code to unblock engineering.

  • User Obsession and Understanding: Talks to experts, operators, and finance partners frequently, and knows how to conduct real user research.

  • Balance of Metrics & Vision: Equally comfortable running rigorous experiments and pushing forward visionary bets.

Benefits

  • Bi-annual performance bonus structure

  • Generous equity grant vested over 4 years

  • Up to $15k Relocation bonus

  • $10K housing bonus (if you live within 0.5 miles of our office)

  • $1.5K monthly stipend for meals

  • Free Equinox membership

  • $200 monthly laundry reimbursement

  • $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement

  • Health, Dental, Vision insurance

jobs.descriptionHtml:

We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

About the Role

We're looking for a strong engineer who can build agentic products that scale. You will work with:

  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, Django, Pydantic

  • Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind

  • Data: PostgreSQL, MySQL, Snowflake, DuckDB, Redis

  • Orchestration/Infra: Kubernetes, Temporal, Modal, Woz

  • Agents/LLM: LangGraph, LangChain, FastMCP, Harbor, NemoGym

  • Observability: Datadog, PostHog, LangSmith

At the end of the process, you’ll be team-matched to where you can have the most impact, on one of the following:

  • Automation – We build intelligent systems and agents that automate operational work at scale—handling talent management, decision-making insights, and knowledge access—so humans can focus on higher-level thinking.This is a newly formed, CEO-facing team focused on 0→1 product development, with a strong emphasis on business impact. The work is highly cross-functional, touching nearly every system across the company.

  • Studio – We own Mercor’s evaluation system & annotation platform for RL environments and tasks. We build harnesses, agents, verifiers, and the end-to-end infrastructure for producing frontier data. Our mission is to scale up high quality RL environments/tasks and expand their capabilities. We work closely with researchers at frontier AI labs to jointly shape the direction of next-generation models.

What You’ll Do

  • Own agentic features end-to-end — from scoping with researchers/ops partners through implementation, launch, and iteration on real customer feedback.

  • Design and ship LLM agents, harnesses, and verifiers — including the tools, prompts, and policies that make them reliable.

  • Build the Python/FastAPI services and Temporal/Modal pipelines that orchestrate agent runs, human-in-the-loop review and iterations.

  • Build state of the art RL environments that expand the capabilities of frontier agents, with realistic enterprise apps, simulated coworkers, and rich company data rooms that support tasks spanning hours to days.

  • Build tooling that turns agent trajectories into insight, from statistical analysis to automated failure mode detection.

  • Build and refine the full-stack surfaces and data infrastructure — craft Next.js/React interfaces where operators and experts work with agents, evolve data models to give agents the structured context and audit trails they need.

  • Define agent quality and drive continuous improvement — build evals, instrument traces, analyze failure modes, and iterate on prompts, tools, and guardrails while raising the bar for reliability, cost, latency, and UX.

  • Partner cross-functionally to shape agent autonomy — work with Product, Design, Research and Ops to draw the lines between autonomous action, propose-and-approve flows, and human-in-the-loop decisions.

Why Mercor

  • Impact: Your work powers how the world’s leading AI labs train and test their models.

  • Learning: Get early insights into frontier model capabilities months before the market.

  • Growth: Work on both infrastructure and research-adjacent projects with fast paths to ownership.

Benefits

  • Bi-annual performance bonus structure

  • Generous equity grant vested over 4 years

  • Up to $15k Relocation bonus

  • $10K housing bonus (if you live within 0.5 miles of our office)

  • $1.5K monthly stipend for meals

  • Free Equinox membership

  • $200 monthly laundry reimbursement

  • $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement

  • Health, Dental, Vision insurance

jobs.title: Research Scientist, APEX Benchmarks
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Mercor

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.

 

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Research Scientist to lead the design of the next generation of APEX benchmarks and the expert-built datasets behind them.

APEX is the AI Productivity Index: a family of benchmarks that measures whether frontier models can do economically valuable professional work. APEX-1 covers single-turn tasks across investment banking, corporate law, consulting and medicine. APEX-Agents tests multi-hour, cross-application agentic work in real tools. APEX-Accounting and APEX-SWE extend that into accounting and real-world software engineering. Every task is written and graded by practicing experts on the Mercor platform, and the results are published as papers, open datasets, and public leaderboards that frontier labs watch.

This is a highly visible role at the intersection of research, company strategy, and go-to-market. You’ll decide what to measure next based on where frontier models are actually failing, design the benchmark and its scoring, work with academic and industry partners to build it, then partner with data operations, product and GTM to scale production. You’ll also be a credible technical voice externally — with labs, partners, prospects and the broader research community.

Mercor is still early on the research side. Much of the methodology, tooling and publishing practice we need does not exist yet. We’re looking for someone who wants to build it.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Benchmark design: Decide what the next APEX benchmark should measure, based on frontier model performance, saturation of existing evals, and where economically valuable work is still out of reach. Own the task taxonomy, difficulty calibration, contamination controls and statistical design.

  • Dataset design: Design expert-built datasets and grading rubrics at scale — deciding what makes a task hard, what makes a grade defensible, and how to hold quality while thousands of experts produce work in parallel.

  • Measurement rigor: Set the standard for how we report results: confidence intervals, inter-rater agreement, human vs. model-as-judge calibration, held-out splits, and the failure analysis that explains why a model scored the way it did.

  • Partnerships: Work with academic collaborators and industry partners (as we did with Cognition on APEX-SWE) to co-design benchmarks and get them adopted.

  • External research voice: Publish — arXiv papers, open datasets, blog posts, conference talks, leaderboard releases — and represent Mercor’s research in conversations with frontier labs, customers and the press.

  • Translate results into narrative: Turn benchmark findings into clear arguments about the ROI of expert-curated data, for technical reports, customer conversations and go-to-market material.

  • Cross-functional work: Partner with data operations, engineering, product and strategy to take a benchmark from design to production, and to surface research findings that shape the company roadmap.

  • Stay at the frontier: Track the LLM evaluation literature and bring what’s good into how Mercor builds benchmarks.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

  • Research background in evaluation: Strong applied or academic research background in LLM evaluation, benchmarking, NLP or a related field, with a track record of rigorous experimental design.

  • Judgment about what to measure: You can look at a frontier model’s behavior and identify the measurement that would actually be informative, rather than the one that is easiest to build.

  • Statistical rigor: You reason carefully about sampling, variance, contamination and grader reliability, and you don’t ship a number you can’t defend.

  • Hands-on: Strong coding skills. You can build an eval harness, run the experiment and analyze the results yourself.

  • Exceptional communication: You can present complex technical findings clearly to frontier lab researchers and to non-technical audiences, in writing and in person.

  • Comfort with ambiguity: You’ve operated in fast-moving, cross-functional environments where the problem space is not yet defined.

  • Interest in the commercial side: Genuine curiosity about GTM strategy, startup dynamics and the business of AI data — this role sits close to all three.

  • In-person: You are excited to work from our San Francisco office five days a week in a high-intensity, high-ownership environment.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Ph.D. in machine learning, NLP or a related field; equivalent industry or frontier lab research experience considered.

  • Publications at top-tier venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ACL, ICLR), especially in evaluation, benchmarking or data-centric AI.

  • Experience authoring a widely-adopted public benchmark or dataset.

  • Industry experience on an evaluation, benchmarking or post-training team at a frontier lab.

  • Domain depth in one of APEX’s professional verticals — finance, law, consulting, accounting, medicine or software engineering.

  • Experience designing rubrics, model-as-judge pipelines, or human annotation programs at scale.

BENEFITS

  • Bi-annual performance bonus structure

  • Generous equity grant vested over 4 years

  • Up to $15k Relocation bonus

  • $10K housing bonus (if you live within 0.5 miles of our office)

  • $1.5K monthly stipend for meals

  • Free Equinox membership

  • $200 monthly laundry reimbursement

  • $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement

  • Health, Dental, Vision insurance

  • 401(k) with company match

WHY MERCOR

APEX results are read by the labs building the models. You’ll decide what the industry measures next, publish it under your own name, and see it move the conversation within weeks rather than years — with the expert network, capital and engineering support to build benchmarks nobody else can.

 - Measurement rigor: Set the standard for how we report results: confidence intervals, inter-rater agreement, human vs. model-as-judge calibration, held-out splits, and the failure analysis that explains why a model scored the way it did.

 - Partnerships: Work with academic collaborators and industry partners (as we did with Cognition on APEX-SWE) to co-design benchmarks and get them adopted.

 - External research voice: Publish — arXiv papers, open datasets, blog posts, conference talks, leaderboard releases — and represent Mercor’s research in conversations with frontier labs, customers and the press.

 - Translate results into narrative: Turn benchmark findings into clear arguments about the ROI of expert-curated data, for technical reports, customer conversations and go-to-market material.

 - Cross-functional work: Partner with data operations, engineering, product and strategy to take a benchmark from design to production, and to surface research findings that shape the company roadmap.

 - Stay at the frontier: Track the LLM evaluation literature and bring what’s good into how Mercor builds benchmarks.






WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Research background in evaluation: Strong applied or academic research background in LLM evaluation, benchmarking, NLP or a related field, with a track record of rigorous experimental design.

 - Judgment about what to measure: You can look at a frontier model’s behavior and identify the measurement that would actually be informative, rather than the one that is easiest to build.

 - Statistical rigor: You reason carefully about sampling, variance, contamination and grader reliability, and you don’t ship a number you can’t defend.

 - Hands-on: Strong coding skills. You can build an eval harness, run the experiment and analyze the results yourself.

 - Exceptional communication: You can present complex technical findings clearly to frontier lab researchers and to non-technical audiences, in writing and in person.

 - Comfort with ambiguity: You’ve operated in fast-moving, cross-functional environments where the problem space is not yet defined.

 - Interest in the commercial side: Genuine curiosity about GTM strategy, startup dynamics and the business of AI data — this role sits close to all three.

 - In-person: You are excited to work from our San Francisco office five days a week in a high-intensity, high-ownership environment.




NICE TO HAVE

 - Ph.D. in machine learning, NLP or a related field; equivalent industry or frontier lab research experience considered.

 - Publications at top-tier venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ACL, ICLR), especially in evaluation, benchmarking or data-centric AI.

 - Experience authoring a widely-adopted public benchmark or dataset.

 - Industry experience on an evaluation, benchmarking or post-training team at a frontier lab.

 - Domain depth in one of APEX’s professional verticals — finance, law, consulting, accounting, medicine or software engineering.

 - Experience designing rubrics, model-as-judge pipelines, or human annotation programs at scale.




BENEFITS

 - Bi-annual performance bonus structure

 - Generous equity grant vested over 4 years

 - Up to $15k Relocation bonus

 - $10K housing bonus (if you live within 0.5 miles of our office)

 - $1.5K monthly stipend for meals

 - Free Equinox membership

 - $200 monthly laundry reimbursement

 - $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement

 - Health, Dental, Vision insurance

 - 401(k) with company match




WHY MERCOR

APEX results are read by the labs building the models. You’ll decide what the industry measures next, publish it under your own name, and see it move the conversation within weeks rather than years — with the expert network, capital and engineering support to build benchmarks nobody else can.

About the Role

This is a high-ownership, deeply technical role. You’ll work through ill-defined problems, prototype quickly with researchers and customers, and take systems from early experiments to reliable, scalable production. You’ll own projects end-to-end: spanning requirements gathering, creating data creation pipelines, and improving model-adjacent infrastructure, while partnering closely with frontier AI labs and Mercor’s internal teams to ship high-impact applied AI solutions.

What You’ll Do

  • Partner closely with frontier AI labs to understand their data, post-training, and evaluation needs

  • Build and operate scalable data pipelines for post-training workflows and model evaluations

  • Design and build scalable systems for synthetic data generation and data quality, and work directly with customers to understand requirements and develop technical solutions

  • Prototype new data types, benchmarks, and evaluation frameworks

  • Lead technical discussions with customers

What Makes This Role Different

  • Direct frontier exposure. You’ll work closely with researchers at leading AI labs, building infrastructure that directly accelerates cutting-edge research.

  • Coding + customer work. This role blends deep technical execution with customer interaction. Engineers who enjoy both building and communicating tend to thrive.

  • Fast-moving, high-ownership environment

  • Technically demanding, collaborative work

  • “Building the plane while flying it”

  • In-person culture at our new New York office at One World Trade Center

  • Aligned with frontier research timelines

What We’re Looking For

  • Strong backend engineering fundamentals in a modern language (Python, Go, Rust, etc.)

  • Experience with model training and inference

  • Strong grounding in statistical analysis and experimental design for measuring model performance and improvements

  • Familiarity with evaluation methods for large language models

  • Comfort working through ambiguity and shipping iteratively

You’re likely someone who

  • Enjoys ownership and customer-facing problem solving

  • Balances speed with engineering rigor

  • Communicates clearly with technical and non-technical users

Why Engineers Join

  • Fast feedback loops and high leverage

  • There are very few roles that combine this level of technical rigor, customer proximity, and research exposure.

We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

We are now building our team in Mexico. This is an opportunity to join Mercor at the beginning of our expansion in Mexico, contribute to how the local team takes shape, and work directly on global projects with some of the world’s most advanced AI companies.

About the Role

The world’s leading AI companies partner with Mercor to execute high-impact projects involving human expertise and data. As a Strategic Project Lead, you will own these projects end to end, build strong customer relationships, and lead the teams responsible for delivering exceptional results.

You will supervise Strategic Project Associates and coordinate large networks of domain experts. SPLs can be responsible for project portfolios generating more than $10 million in annual revenue and involving over 1,000 contributors.

This is a hands-on leadership role for ambitious professionals who enjoy solving complex problems, developing people, and turning challenging goals into results. It offers the opportunity to take on significant responsibility, accelerate your growth, and have a tangible impact on AI - the defining industry of our time.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead high-impact projects for some of the world’s leading AI labs and technology companies.

  • Own projects, from customer conversations through successful delivery.

  • Turn complex customer needs into clear plans and help teams execute them effectively.

  • Lead and develop Strategic Project Associates, helping them grow and perform at a high level.

  • Coordinate large groups of domain experts across fields such as software engineering, medicine, law, science, and business.

  • Build trusted relationships with customers and serve as a primary point of contact.

  • Use data and structured problem-solving to understand performance, identify challenges, and improve results.

  • Ensure that projects consistently meet high standards for quality, speed, and customer experience.

  • Collaborate with Operations, Engineering, and Machine Learning teams to develop better ways of working.

  • Identify opportunities to expand successful projects and create additional value for customers.

What We’re Looking For

  • 3 - 6+ years of professional experience.

  • Experience owning and delivering complex projects in fast-moving or demanding environments.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to bring structure to unfamiliar or ambiguous challenges.

  • Experience managing people, leading teams, or coordinating multiple stakeholders toward a shared goal.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English. You will work directly with international colleagues, customers, and experts.

  • Strong analytical skills and comfort using data to understand problems and make decisions.

  • Intellectual curiosity and a genuine interest in understanding how data, technology, and AI systems work.

  • The ability to prioritize effectively and manage several important workstreams at the same time.

  • Confidence working with customers and the judgment to communicate progress, challenges, and recommendations clearly.

  • Ambition and a strong desire to learn, grow, and take on increasing responsibility.

  • Excitement about contributing to AI and having a meaningful impact on one of the world’s most important and rapidly evolving industries.

  • Initiative, adaptability, low ego, and openness to feedback.

  • Enthusiasm for using AI tools, combined with the critical thinking needed to evaluate their output.

Experience in startups, consulting, strategy and operations, product, engineering, data, technology, entrepreneurship, Chief of Staff roles, customer-facing positions, or people management can be valuable. No single professional background is required; demonstrated ownership, leadership, learning ability, and execution matter most.

Technical or coding experience is not required, but candidates should be comfortable working with data, learning new systems, and developing an understanding of AI-enabled workflows.

Why Join Mercor?

Mercor offers the opportunity to accelerate your career inside a profitable, high-growth U.S. technology startup at the forefront of AI.

You will work in a fast-paced and high-intensity environment where projects move quickly, standards are high, and your decisions can have a visible impact on customers, teams, and the business. You will gain exposure to complex global projects, lead talented people, and grow alongside Mercor’s expanding team in Mexico.

This role is particularly well suited to ambitious people who want to challenge themselves, grow as operators and leaders, and help shape an industry that will transform how people and companies work.

Location

This role is currently remote and is intended for candidates based in Mexico City.

Mercor plans to open an office in Mexico City as the team grows. The role is expected to transition to an in-person working model once the office opens. Joining now means becoming one of the early contributors to Mercor’s presence and culture in Mexico.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Competitive salary.

  • Performance-based bonus structure.

  • Meaningful equity ownership in a high-growth U.S. technology company.

  • Benefits above those required by Mexican law.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Mercor

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

What This Person Owns

The infrastructure every data-driven team at Mercor runs on: Snowflake, Fivetran, Airflow, and Hex. You own how data is organized, who can access what, what it costs to run, and how reliably it operates. This is a foundational hire on a new Data Platform team, you'll help set the standards other engineers build against.

What They Do Day-to-Day

- Bring structure and clear ownership to how data is organized in Snowflake across projects and teams

- Design narrow, role-based access controls, and partner with automation so access is granted and revoked as people join, change teams, or leave

- Extend row access policies and PII masking across all sensitive datasets

- Migrate data from a variety of vendor and internal sources into properly owned, governed homes

- Own Fivetran connector health and cost, Airflow/Astronomer pipeline reliability and on-call, and Hex governance across company-wide dashboards

- Monitor and right-size Snowflake warehouse spend

- Help build CDC/streaming ingestion and other internal data platform tooling

What We're Looking For

- Hands-on experience with Snowflake administration: roles, grants, warehouses, cost/performance tuning

- Experience designing data access and governance models (RBAC, row-level security, PII) at scale

- Comfort owning vendor tooling end to end (Fivetran, Airflow/Astronomer, or similar), including on-call

- Track record migrating or re-architecting live production data systems without breaking dependent teams

- Strong SQL and Python, with infrastructure fluency to make judgment calls, not just execute a spec

- Experience owning CDC/streaming pipelines in production (Debezium, Kafka, Snowpipe Streaming or similar), including reasoning about delivery semantics, partitioning, and safe cutovers between systems.

Benefits

  • Bi-annual performance bonus structure

  • Generous equity grant vested over 4 years

  • Up to $15k Relocation bonus

  • $10K housing bonus (if you live within 0.5 miles of our office)

  • $1.5K monthly stipend for meals

  • $200 monthly laundry reimbursement

  • $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement

  • Collaborate closely with Strategic Project Leads, Operations, Engineering, and Machine Learning teams to meet customer objectives.

  • Design and improve processes that enable projects to operate more accurately, efficiently, and at greater scale.

  • Identify opportunities to expand successful projects and create additional value for customers.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Strategic Project Associate, you will work closely with Strategic Project Leads to execute large-scale projects for leading AI labs and technology companies.



You will help manage project portfolios representing millions of dollars in revenue, coordinate hundreds of highly skilled domain experts, identify and resolve operational and data-quality issues, and ensure that projects consistently meet a high standard.



This is not a traditional entry-level project coordination role. You will have the opportunity to take ownership, make sound decisions with incomplete information, move quickly, and contribute directly to the success of high-impact customer programs.



The role offers significant responsibility early in your career, exposure to the frontier of AI, and rapid growth opportunities within a fast-paced U.S. startup.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Execute complex, large-scale projects on behalf of leading AI labs and technology companies.

 - Help manage multimillion-dollar project portfolios, ensuring strong delivery, quality, and customer outcomes.

 - Source, evaluate, onboard, and manage the performance of hundreds of domain experts across areas such as software engineering, medicine, law, science, business, and others.

 - Monitor project performance and investigate operational or data-quality issues before they affect delivery.

 - Develop a strong understanding of why the data matters, what quality means for each project, and how project decisions can influence AI model performance.

 - Anticipate blockers, prioritize competing needs, and take initiative without waiting for detailed instructions.

 - Build strong working relationships with customers and communicate progress, risks, and recommendations clearly.

 - Collaborate closely with Strategic Project Leads, Operations, Engineering, and Machine Learning teams to meet customer objectives.

 - Design and improve processes that enable projects to operate more accurately, efficiently, and at greater scale.

 - Identify opportunities to expand successful projects and create additional value for customers.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 0 - 3 years of professional experience. New graduates looking for their first full-time professional opportunity are encouraged to apply.

 - Strong analytical thinking and an ability to identify patterns, inconsistencies, and root causes.

 - Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to approach unfamiliar challenges with structure, creativity, and sound judgment.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English. You will work with international colleagues, customers, and experts.

 - Intellectual curiosity and a genuine interest in understanding how systems, data, and AI models work.

 - A high level of ownership, urgency, and attention to detail.

 - The ability to prioritize effectively and manage several workstreams at the same time.

 - Comfort operating in ambiguous situations, making decisions, and adjusting quickly as circumstances change.

 - Enthusiasm for using AI tools, combined with the critical thinking necessary to evaluate their output.

 - Openness to feedback, and a willingness to address problems directly and transparently.

 - Evidence that you have taken initiative, built something, led others, or assumed meaningful responsibility - whether professionally, academically, or through an entrepreneurial or extracurricular project.

Experience in startups, consulting, strategy and operations, product, engineering, data, technology, entrepreneurship, or customer-facing roles can be valuable, but no single professional background is required.

We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

About the Role

As a Data Science Intern at Mercor, you’ll join a fast-moving, metrics-driven engineering team whose work shapes decisions across the company. You’ll analyze data that directly affects ranking, hiring efficiency, candidate experience and revenue, work with production datasets from your first week, and ship insights that product and engineering act on.

You’ll start on the analyses and tooling your team has wanted but hasn’t had the hands for, and as needs come up you’ll take deep ownership of them, with a named mentor alongside you. You’ll move quickly while keeping a high bar for analytical rigor, clarity and statistical correctness.

Where You’ll Work

Interns start on a rolling basis, so summer, spring and fall terms all work. About three weeks before your start we’ll match you to one of two teams:

  • Product Data Science. The data science function for the marketplace and talent platform: metrics for matching, ranking and hiring efficiency, event instrumentation and data integrity, experiments on the candidate and customer experience, and scoring models that change who gets surfaced for which role.

  • Applied AI Data Science. The data science function inside the org that delivers human data and evaluations to frontier AI labs: operational analytics for live customer projects, automated quality control that gates what ships, and evaluation science that shows a lab where its model breaks and why.

What You’ll Work On

  • Defining north-star metrics and feature-level KPIs for ranking, interview analytics and payouts

  • Designing A/B tests and quasi-experiments and turning results into product decisions within days

  • Building dashboards and lightweight data models so teams can self-serve insights

  • Instrumenting events with engineers and improving data quality, observability and latency

  • Prototyping models, from baselines to gradient boosting, to improve matching and scoring

  • Evaluating LLM-powered systems through rubric design, human-in-the-loop experiments and guardrail testing

What We’re Looking For

  • Pursuing a degree in a quantitative field, graduating 2027 (potentially 2028)

  • Strong fundamentals in statistics, SQL and Python

  • Experience with experiment design, causal reasoning and data analysis

  • Clear communication with engineers, product managers and leadership

  • Curiosity about LLM evaluation, retrieval, ranking or marketplace dynamics

  • Excited to work in person in San Francisco

  • Nice to have: dbt, dashboarding tools, recommendation or search metrics, LLM and agent evaluation

Why Mercor

  • Impact: your work powers how frontier AI labs train and deploy their models

  • Learning: early exposure to frontier AI research and engineering

  • Growth: a high-velocity team where interns ship to production

Compensation and Benefits

  • $10K housing bonus if you live within 0.5 miles of our office during your internship

  • $1.5K monthly stipend for meals/rideshare

  • Health, dental and vision insurance

  • 401(k) eligibility

jobs.title: Chief of Staff, Delivery Operations
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Mercor

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

About the Role

Delivery Operations at Mercor is responsible for the end-to-end execution of our human data programs, ensuring projects are staffed, scoped, and delivered on time and at quality for our customers. We're looking for a Chief of Staff to work directly with the VP of Delivery Operations to drive strategic initiatives, keep cross-functional execution tight, and turn priorities into results across a fast-moving org.

This is a high-visibility role for someone who wants operating experience at the center of a growing business, with direct exposure to how a human data delivery org is run.

Reports to VP, Delivery Operations

What You'll Do

  • Strategic partnership: Act as a thought partner to the VP, helping set priorities, structure decisions, and prepare for key meetings, reviews, and offsites

  • Cross-functional execution: Drive projects from strategy to execution, coordinating across Delivery, Recruiting, Ops, Product, and Finance to keep initiatives on track

  • Operating rhythm: Build and maintain the operating rhythm of the org, including weekly business reviews, KPI tracking, OKRs, and leadership reporting

  • Problem solving: Turn ambiguous problems into structured plans, diagnosing operational bottlenecks and proposing fixes across staffing, throughput, quality, and margin

  • Executive communication: Prepare briefings, decks, and analyses for exec and board-level conversations

  • Special projects: Own initiatives as they arise, including new program launches, process redesigns, vendor evaluations, and headcount planning

  • Force multiplier: Serve as a trusted filter for the VP, triaging what needs their attention versus what can be delegated or resolved directly

What We're Looking For

  • 2–5 years of experience in a high-ownership operating role, such as chief of staff, business or strategy operations, management consulting, investment banking, venture, or a startup operating role

  • Prior experience in human data, data annotation, RLHF, or AI training data operations

  • Strong analytical skills; comfortable building models, structuring ambiguous problems, and drawing conclusions from data

  • Excellent written and verbal communication; able to synthesize complex information into clear, concise recommendations

  • A bias toward execution; someone who can move from "what should we do" to "it's done" without much hand-holding

  • Comfortable operating in fast-changing, high-growth environments with shifting priorities

  • A track record of excellent cross-functional collaboration, building trust and aligning stakeholders across teams and orgs

Why This Role

You'll sit at the center of one of Mercor's most operationally intensive functions, with a direct line to strategic decision-making and a fast path to broader ownership as the org scales.

jobs.title: Mercor AI Safety Fund Grants
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Mercor

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.

 

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

Mercor Safety Research Grants $5M

One of the biggest challenges the industry faces today is addressing whether frontier AI is safe enough to deploy. A model can pass safety checks and still act differently in production. This is why investing today in safety research, evals and verification is critical.

Mercor is committing $5 million to fund safety research. Award size and mix depend on the project. The grant supports:

  • Researcher hours

  • API costs

  • Stipends for event and conference attendance

  • The time of experts from Mercor's platform

This is separate from the Mercor Research Fellowship, which funds benchmark and economics work. You can apply to that HERE.

What we're looking for

We're open to proposals across the full range of safety interests. We're particularly interested in:

  • Misalignment: deceptive alignment, goal misgeneralization, reward hacking, scheming, and situationally-aware failure modes

  • Sandbox escape: containment failures, privilege escalation, tool misuse, and agents operating outside their intended scope

  • Evaluation awareness: models detecting they are being tested and behaving differently under observation than in deployment

  • Interpretability: understanding what models are actually doing internally, and whether that can be made legible to a human reviewer

  • Oversight and control: scalable supervision, human-in-the-loop reliability, and what breaks when the system is more capable than its reviewer

  • Red-teaming methodology: more robust systems for uncovering novel failures

If your work doesn't fit neatly into these, apply anyway. Strong proposals outside this list are welcome.

Why us

  • Funding for researcher time, API costs, and event attendance

  • Where useful to the work: access to Mercor's expert network for human grading, red-teaming, and annotation: lawyers, accountants, engineers, scientists, clinicians

  • Access to Mercor's internal evaluation infrastructure, subject to review

  • Introductions to Mercor's network of researchers across frontier labs and academia

Who should apply

  • Researchers at universities and non-profit research organizations, as well as public benefit corporations and small startups that do not sell AI training data. Awards are made to the researcher’s institution.

  • People with a specific, well-scoped question: the grant is built around your proposal, not a generic research rotation

  • Applicants based in the United States or the United Kingdom

  • Background in ML, CS, statistics, or an adjacent field (measurement, psychometrics, HCI, security, social science)

  • Bonus: experience with agentic evaluation, RL environments, adversarial ML, or systems security

We expect grantees to publish. A paper, an open dataset, a public methodology, or a tool the field can use, released under an open license that permits commercial use.

Award terms

Selected grantees will sign Mercor’s research award agreement. Key terms include:

  • Grantees keep ownership of their work and grant Mercor a non-exclusive license to use it, including commercially.

  • Mercor may identify grantees and their institutions as award recipients, including by name and logo. Grantees may use Mercor’s logo with Mercor’s approval.

  • For benchmark and evaluation projects, Mercor receives early access to the benchmark before public release and the exclusive right to build and host a private held-out test set, at Mercor’s cost.

  • Grantees agree not to work with specified Mercor competitors on substantially similar benchmarks or evaluations during the award and for 12 months afterward.

  • Grantees are free to publish their findings. Mercor reviews drafts in advance only to remove its confidential information.

  • Awards are subject to tax documentation, sanctions screening, and periodic progress reports.

How to apply

Submit an Expression of Interest. We expect to see a one- or two-page document. It should contain at least a section on your team, background, and research accomplishments; a section on your proposed research project; and a section on the outputs and impact of the project, with directionally correct timelines and resource requirements. Please do not include confidential or proprietary information in your Expression of Interest. Submitting an Expression of Interest does not obligate Mercor to make an award.

You’ll start on the work your team has wanted to do but hasn’t had the hands for, and as needs come up you’ll take deep ownership of them, with a named mentor alongside you. You’ll work closely with product and design, move fast, and hold a high bar for quality, scalability and simplicity.



Where You’ll Work

Interns start on a rolling basis, so summer, spring and fall terms all work. About six weeks before your start we’ll match you to the team where you’ll have the most impact, across one of the engineering sub-departments: 

 - Talent platform. The marketplace that sources, vets, matches and pays expert talent.

 - Applied AI. Delivery systems, quality control and evals for the human data we ship to frontier labs.

 - Agents. Internal agents that automate operational work across the company.

 - Platform engineering. Shared infrastructure, contracts, payments and reliability.

 - Studio. The platform for creating and analyzing datasets.



What We’re Looking For

 - Pursuing a degree in Computer Science or a related field, graduating 2027 to 2029

 - Strong programming skills in Python, Go or TypeScript

 - Solid grounding in data structures, algorithms and systems

 - Experience with APIs, SQL or NoSQL databases and cloud platforms

 - Curiosity about AI and an interest in startups

 - Excited to work in person in San Francisco
   
   

Why Mercor

 - Impact: your work powers how frontier AI labs train and deploy their models

 - Learning: early exposure to frontier AI research and engineering

 - Growth: a high-velocity team where interns ship to production
   
   

Compensation and Benefits

 - $10K housing bonus if you live within 0.5 miles of our office during your internship

 - $1.5K monthly stipend for meals/rideshare

 - Health, dental and vision insurance

 - 401(k) eligibility

jobs.title: Senior HR Business Partner, Delivery
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Mercor

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Senior HR Business Partner to support Mercor’s Delivery organization.

Delivery sits at the center of how Mercor turns customer demand into high-quality human data. Teams are launching and scaling accounts quickly, managing changing customer requirements, developing operators into larger roles, and making constant decisions about talent, performance and organizational structure.

The HRBP supporting this organization needs to understand that environment.

You will work directly with Delivery leaders and managers on the people decisions that affect whether an account and the organization perform: who we put in critical roles, how we develop strong operators, where management is breaking down, how teams should be structured, when someone needs a larger challenge, and when performance is below the bar.

This is not a role for someone who wants to operate at a distance from the business. You should understand the work, the customer environment and the economics well enough to challenge leaders and make practical recommendations.

Experience in the human data / AI data industry is required. You should already understand the operating model behind businesses delivering human-generated data, expert data, model evaluations, RLHF, data annotation or similar services to AI customers.

What You’ll Do

  • Partner directly with Delivery leadership. Advise leaders on talent, organization design, management, performance and workforce decisions as the organization scales.

  • Get close to the accounts. Understand the differences between teams, customers and types of work so that your people recommendations reflect the actual business rather than a generic HR model.

  • Raise the performance bar. Help managers distinguish exceptional performance from strong performance and performance that is below the bar. Make sure decisions are grounded in evidence and addressed quickly.

  • Develop strong operators. Identify high-performing SPLs, account leaders and other critical talent early. Work with leaders to create meaningful next opportunities through larger accounts, expanded scope, new problems, internal mobility or management opportunities.

  • Strengthen managers. Coach managers on feedback, expectations, team effectiveness, difficult conversations, performance issues and leadership behavior. Step in when a manager needs direct challenge, not simply support.

  • Help us retain our best people. Identify retention risk before it becomes a resignation. Understand what is driving it, including scope, compensation, manager quality, account experience, career progression and external market pull, and work with leaders on the right intervention.

  • Shape the organization as it changes. Partner on role clarity, organization design, succession, spans and layers, leadership changes and movement of talent between teams and accounts.

  • Bring a people lens to staffing and workload. Identify when persistent workload, account design, insufficient capacity or operating friction is becoming a talent problem and work with Delivery leadership to address the root cause.

  • Handle difficult people situations well. Support leaders through performance concerns, conduct issues, organizational changes, role changes and exits with speed, consistency and good judgment.

  • Run talent and performance mechanisms for Delivery. Make the company-wide approach usable in a fast-moving operating organization without turning it into unnecessary process.

  • See patterns before they become bigger problems. Use talent, performance, retention and employee signals to tell Delivery leadership what is changing and where intervention is needed.

  • Build what does not exist yet. Mercor is still early. When the business needs a new mechanism, manager tool or talent practice, you should be comfortable building the first version yourself and improving it through use.

What We’re Looking For

  • Human data industry experience is required. You have worked inside a company delivering human data or human expertise for AI systems, including areas such as AI training data, expert data, RLHF, model evaluation, data annotation or labeling, or closely related human data operations. You understand how these businesses actually run.

  • 8+ years of strong HRBP experience. You have been the primary People partner to senior leaders and can independently handle complex organizational and talent decisions.

  • Experience with operations or delivery organizations. You have supported teams where performance is closely tied to customers, quality, speed, capacity and execution.

  • High-growth startup experience. You are comfortable with rapid organizational change, incomplete systems, ambiguous ownership and a business that can look meaningfully different six months from now.

  • Strong business judgment. You can understand what is happening operationally, separate symptoms from root causes and make a clear recommendation.

  • High performance orientation. You are comfortable differentiating performance, investing disproportionately in exceptional people and addressing weak performance directly.

  • Excellent manager coach. You can make managers better and are comfortable challenging experienced leaders when their management approach is contributing to the problem.

  • Strong talent instinct. You can recognize people with unusual trajectory, understand what may cause them to leave and help create opportunities that keep them growing.

  • 0→1 builder. You have created useful talent, manager or organizational practices where little infrastructure existed before.

  • Operator mindset. You do not stop at identifying the problem or writing the recommendation. You stay close enough to the work to make sure the solution actually works.

  • Direct and low ego. You communicate clearly, handle disagreement well and care more about reaching the right answer than protecting your own idea.

  • In-person. You are able to work from our San Francisco office five days a week.

Why Mercor

This role has unusual proximity to the core business.

You will work with the leaders responsible for delivering some of Mercor’s most important customer work while helping shape the talent systems behind an organization that is scaling extremely quickly.

You will have the opportunity to influence how we identify and develop exceptional operators, build stronger managers, structure Delivery teams, retain critical talent and raise the performance bar across the organization.

For someone who already understands the human data industry, this is an opportunity to help build the People infrastructure for one of the companies defining its next stage.

jobs.title: Research Scientist - Environments, Data and Post-Training
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Mercor

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.

 

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

About the Role

As a Research Scientist at Mercor, you will work at the intersection of research and engineering on frontier post-training. You will develop new training and evaluation methods, test them through rigorous experiments, and implement successful approaches at scale.

Working with researchers, engineers, domain experts, and customers, you will investigate how data, rewards, environments, and optimization methods shape model behavior. Your work will influence frontier models, Mercor’s products, and the broader research community through releasing blogposts, technical reports, and papers.

What You’ll Do

  • Implement novel post-training methods that improve model reasoning, tool use, and agentic behavior.

  • Develop new training recipes for frontier open models.

  • Design and run experiments across datasets, reward functions, environments, and optimization strategies, including methods such as GRPO and DAPO.

  • Build reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) and other post-training pipelines at scale.

  • Investigate model capabilities and failure modes, then develop targeted training interventions.

  • Create methods for measuring data quality, usability, and causal impact on model performance.

  • Build scalable pipelines for data generation, filtering, augmentation, and selection.

  • Develop rubrics, evaluators, benchmarks, and scoring systems that inform training decisions.

  • Translate open-ended research questions into rigorous experiments and production systems.

  • Collaborate with researchers, applied AI teams, engineers, and domain experts producing training data.

  • Contribute to open-source post-training tools and research.

What We’re Looking For

  • Demonstrated experience training and evaluating machine learning models.

  • A strong research record in post-training, reinforcement learning, language-model evaluation, data-centric ML, or a closely related field.

  • Ability to reason rigorously about model behavior, experimental results, and data quality.

  • Strong programming skills and experience implementing machine learning systems.

  • Knowledge of the current AI research landscape and important open problems.

  • Excitement to work in person in San Francisco, five days a week (with optional remote Saturdays), and thrive in a high-intensity, high-ownership environment.

Nice To Have

  • Experience on an industry post-training or frontier-model team.

  • Main authorship of publications at top-tier conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ACL).

  • Experience with synthetic-data generation

  • Experience building large-scale evaluation or data-generation infrastructure.

  • Solid foundations in distributed or backend systems, and experimental design.

  • Familiarity with APIs, databases, and cloud infrastructure.

Benefits

  • Bi-annual performance bonus structure

  • Generous equity grant vested over 4 years

  • Up to $15k Relocation bonus

  • $10K housing bonus (if you live within 0.5 miles of our office)

  • $1.5K monthly stipend for meals

  • Free Equinox membership

  • $200 monthly laundry reimbursement

  • $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement

  • Health, Dental, Vision insurance

jobs.title: Mercor AI Research Fund Grants: Benchmarks
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Mercor

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.

 

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

Mercor AI Research Fund Grants: Benchmarks

One of the biggest challenges facing the industry today is determining whether frontier AI is capable enough to deliver value in real-world settings. A model can perform well on benchmarks and still struggle in production. That’s why investing in research, realistic evaluations, and robust verification is critical.

Mercor is seeking to fund AI research on benchmarking. This is separate from the Mercor Research Fellowship, which funds individual experts (apply HERE), our $5m of safety funding awards (apply HERE), and our research funding on the economic impacts of AI.

The grant supports:

  • The time of experts from Mercor's platform

  • Researcher hours

  • API costs

  • Stipends for event and conference attendance

Budget Categories

Applications are grouped into three budget tiers. Please state your tier clearly in your application and ensure your overall budget ask falls within it:

  • Tier 1: under $50,000: Suited to focused, well-scoped projects such as pilot studies, evaluations, replications, or extensions of existing work. These applications undergo a streamlined review.

  • Tier 2: under $200,000: Suited to substantial projects requiring dedicated personnel time, meaningful compute, or data collection. Reviewed with proportionally greater attention to the budget breakdown and implementation plan.

  • Tier 3: under $500,000: Reserved for ambitious, multi-component research programs. These applications receive the highest level of scrutiny: reviewers will expect a detailed justification of each spend category, a clear account of team capacity to execute at this scale, and milestones against which progress can be assessed.

The level of review scrutiny scales with the size of the ask, so applicants should request the smallest budget that credibly supports the proposed work.

 

Research Agenda

 

We are interested in submissions in the following area:

  • Real-world evaluations: measuring whether benchmark performance translates into reliable performance on realistic tasks and workflows

  • Environments: building high-fidelity, interactive environments that capture the complexity of real-world work

  • Long-horizon tasks: evaluating and improving models’ ability to plan, execute, and adapt across extended workflows

  • Agentic capabilities: tool use, coordination, memory, and autonomous execution

  • Reasoning and problem-solving: improving performance on complex, ambiguous, or underspecified tasks

  • Post-training: developing better data, rewards, and training methods to improve model capabilities

  • Evaluation methodology: creating more robust measures of capability, reliability, and real-world utility

Eligibility

  • Researchers at universities and non-profit research organizations, as well as public benefit corporations and small startups (<20 people) that do not sell AI training data. Awards are made to the researcher’s institution.

  • Applicants must be based in the United States or the United Kingdom

We expect grantees to publish a paper, an open dataset, a public methodology, or a tool the field can use, released under an open license that permits commercial use.

 

Timeline

 

  • Application deadline: November 27, 2026, 11:59 PM PT (UTC−8)

  • Notification to applicants: by December 18, 2026

Late or incomplete applications will not be reviewed. All applicants will be notified of the outcome whether or not they are shortlisted.

 
 

How to apply

We invite interested researchers to submit a brief Expression of Interest (EOI) before preparing a full proposal. The EOI should be ~1–3 pages and include:

  • Research question and background (max 250 words): What are you trying to do? State your objective in plain language, with minimal jargon. How is this problem addressed today, and what are the limits of current practice? Who cares: if you succeed, what difference will it make, and to whom?

  • Project proposal (max 400 words): Concrete technical and implementation detail: your approach, methods, datasets, models, compute, and evaluation plan.

  • Novelty (max 200 words): What is new in your approach relative to existing and ongoing work, and why do you believe it will succeed where current practice falls short?

  • Risks (max 150 words): What are the main technical and execution risks, and how will you mitigate or detect them early?

  • Team (max 100 words; if the team is large, up to 200): The researchers on the project and their relevant background and prior work.

  • Proposed outcomes and timeline: Expected deliverables (papers, artifacts, datasets, tools) and key milestones, including how long the work will take. Include the mid-term and final “exams”: the checkpoints and success criteria by which we will know whether the project is on track and succeeds.

  • Budget overview: How much will it cost? Provide a specific overall budget ask, your budget tier (see Budget Categories), and a breakdown by spend category (e.g., personnel, compute, data, travel/other).

    • Other sources of funding for this project should be clearly identified in the proposal budget

Guidance for applicants.

  • Strong EOIs are specific rather than high-level: they name the methods, systems, and evaluation criteria they will use, and they engage directly with existing literature and ongoing efforts rather than describing the problem space in general terms.

  • The EOI should briefly establish the PI’s (and key team members’) relevant background and prior work; proposals without demonstrated expertise in the research area are rarely competitive. Researchers with experience with agentic evaluation, RL environments, and post-training are encouraged to apply

  • Proposals that duplicate work already being pursued by many other groups are unlikely to advance unless they offer a clearly differentiated angle.

  • Please do not include confidential or proprietary information in your Expression of Interest. Submitting an Expression of Interest does not obligate Mercor to make an award.

 
 

Award terms

Selected grantees will sign Mercor’s research award agreement. Key terms include:

  • Grantees keep ownership of their work and grant Mercor a non-exclusive license to use it, including commercially.

  • Mercor may identify grantees and their institutions as award recipients, including by name and logo. Grantees may use Mercor’s logo with Mercor’s approval.

  • For benchmark and evaluation projects, Mercor receives early access to the benchmark before public release and the exclusive right to build and host a private held-out test set, at Mercor’s cost.

  • Grantees are free to publish their findings. Mercor reviews drafts in advance only to remove its confidential information.

  • Awards are subject to tax documentation, sanctions screening, and periodic progress reports.

 - Research question and background (max 250 words): What are you trying to do? State your objective in plain language, with minimal jargon. How is this problem addressed today, and what are the limits of current practice? Who cares: if you succeed, what difference will it make, and to whom?

 - Project proposal (max 400 words): Concrete technical and implementation detail: your approach, methods, datasets, models, compute, and evaluation plan.

 - Novelty (max 200 words): What is new in your approach relative to existing and ongoing work, and why do you believe it will succeed where current practice falls short?

 - Risks (max 150 words): What are the main technical and execution risks, and how will you mitigate or detect them early?

 - Team (max 100 words; if the team is large, up to 200): The researchers on the project and their relevant background and prior work.

 - Proposed outcomes and timeline: Expected deliverables (papers, artifacts, datasets, tools) and key milestones, including how long the work will take. Include the mid-term and final “exams”: the checkpoints and success criteria by which we will know whether the project is on track and succeeds.

 - Budget overview: How much will it cost? Provide a specific overall budget ask, your budget tier (see Budget Categories), and a breakdown by spend category (e.g., personnel, compute, data, travel/other).
   
   - Other sources of funding for this project should be clearly identified in the proposal budget




GUIDANCE FOR APPLICANTS.

 - Strong EOIs are specific rather than high-level: they name the methods, systems, and evaluation criteria they will use, and they engage directly with existing literature and ongoing efforts rather than describing the problem space in general terms.

 - The EOI should briefly establish the PI’s (and key team members’) relevant background and prior work; proposals without demonstrated expertise in the research area are rarely competitive. Researchers with experience with agentic evaluation, RL environments, and post-training are encouraged to apply

 - Proposals that duplicate work already being pursued by many other groups are unlikely to advance unless they offer a clearly differentiated angle.

 - Please do not include confidential or proprietary information in your Expression of Interest. Submitting an Expression of Interest does not obligate Mercor to make an award.

 
 


AWARD TERMS

Selected grantees will sign Mercor’s research award agreement. Key terms include:

 - Grantees keep ownership of their work and grant Mercor a non-exclusive license to use it, including commercially.

 - Mercor may identify grantees and their institutions as award recipients, including by name and logo. Grantees may use Mercor’s logo with Mercor’s approval.

 - For benchmark and evaluation projects, Mercor receives early access to the benchmark before public release and the exclusive right to build and host a private held-out test set, at Mercor’s cost.

 - Grantees are free to publish their findings. Mercor reviews drafts in advance only to remove its confidential information.

 - Awards are subject to tax documentation, sanctions screening, and periodic progress reports.

Build the Finance Client Function (0 → 1)

  • Identify, engage, and onboard financial services clients and partners

Account Ownership & Growth

  • Qualify client needs, define mutual value, and drive engagements to close

  • Structure commercial terms suited to financial institutions' procurement and compliance norms

Contracting & Negotiation

  • Own negotiations on pricing, scope, timelines, and obligations with finance clients

  • Work closely with Legal and Finance to move quickly without sacrificing rigor

  • Navigate data rights, compliance, and security requirements specific to financial services

Stakeholder Management

  • Act as the primary point of contact for finance-sector clients and senior stakeholders

  • Manage complex, multi-party relationships (compliance, procurement, technical teams) with clarity and credibility

  • Align internal teams (Product, Research, Ops, Legal) around finance client priorities

Operate Scrappily, Then Systematize

  • Start hands-on: build client lists, run outreach, draft docs, close deals yourself

  • Identify patterns and convert them into repeatable processes as the finance book of business scales

What We're Looking For

Experience

  • 5+ years in Client Service, Account Management, or Commercial roles, serving financial services clients

  • Proven experience negotiating and closing contracts

  • Track record managing high-stakes external stakeholders, including compliance/procurement functions

  • Direct experience working with data products

  • Required: Prior experience working at or directly serving financial services firms, including private equity, venture capital, investment banking, asset management, or other financial institutions.

Mindset & Skills

  • Builder mentality: excited by ambiguity and 0→1 problems

  • Scrappy, resourceful, comfortable with unglamorous work early on

  • Strong commercial instincts and negotiation skills

  • Clear, concise communicator with executive presence

  • Able to operate independently while partnering closely with internal teams

Nice to Have

  • Experience in fintech, banking, asset management, or financial data platforms

  • Background working cross-functionally with legal and finance teams

  • Bi-annual performance bonus structure

  • Generous equity grant vested over 4 years

  • Up to $15k relocation bonus

  • $10K housing bonus (if you live within 0.5 miles of our office)

  • $1.5K monthly stipend for meals

  • Free Equinox membership

  • $200 monthly laundry reimbursement

  • $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement

  • Health, Dental, Vision insurance

jobs.title: Corporate Finance Senior / Associate
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Mercor

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work.
