You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

About the Role

We are looking for a Corporate Finance Senior / Associate to join Mercor's Finance team and help lead the company's core corporate finance activities at our headquarters in San Fransisco.

You will sit at the intersection of nearly every part of Mercor, from our rapidly growing core business to new bets, M&A, capital markets, and other strategic initiatives. You will work closely with leaders across the business, our Business Operations partners, the Data and Automation team, and the broader Finance organization to understand how the company operates and translate those operating drivers into financial outcomes.

You will own and continuously develop Mercor's central corporate financial model and support a broad range of strategic finance priorities, including forecasting, capital allocation, financing and capital markets, M&A, and fundraising. You will also help shape how we communicate Mercor's financial performance and trajectory to investors, lenders, and other external stakeholders.

This is a highly analytical, cross-functional, and autonomous role with significant exposure to Mercor's leadership team. We are looking for someone who can take an ambiguous problem, independently determine how to approach it, and drive a workstream from analysis through execution. Your work will directly influence how Mercor plans, invests, allocates capital, and executes on its next stage of growth.

What You'll Do

  • Own and continuously develop Mercor's central corporate financial model, including forecasts and upside and downside scenarios, and independently identify opportunities to improve how we model the business.

  • Drive company-wide forecasting and budgeting in partnership with Finance, Business Operations, the Data and Automation team, and business leaders.

  • Partner with teams across the business to understand key operating drivers and unit economics, translate them into financial outcomes, and use those insights to improve decision-making and accelerate growth.

  • Support capital markets and financing initiatives, including managing external relationships, fundraising, and executing financing transactions.

  • Support M&A and other strategic transactions from initial evaluation through diligence and execution, including independently driving analyses, diligence workstreams, and cross-functional coordination.

  • Evaluate investments and capital allocation decisions, turning complex financial and operating information into clear recommendations for executive leadership.

  • Take ownership of ambiguous, cross-functional projects, develop the workplan and analytical framework, and drive execution with autonomy.

What We're Looking For

  • 4–6 years of finance experience. Investment banking experience is strongly preferred, particularly in combination with private equity, investing, strategic finance, or operating experience at a high-growth startup.

  • Exceptional financial modeling capabilities. You enjoy the technical work and can independently build detailed, structurally sound models from the ground up, while exercising good judgment about when a quick analysis is enough.

  • High agency, resourcefulness, and intellectual curiosity. You are a self-starter who can take a loosely defined objective, determine what needs to happen, and drive it forward without waiting for a playbook.

  • Strong strategic judgment. You can step back from the details, understand the underlying business question, and focus your analysis on the decisions and outputs that matter most.

  • Strong understanding of financing structures, capital allocation, and how financial decisions affect the broader business.

  • Exceptional project management, cross-functional, and communication skills. You can manage complex workstreams, coordinate across a large number of stakeholders, navigate ambiguity and shifting priorities, build strong external relationships, present directly to executive leadership, and drive projects from idea through execution.

Benefits

  • $15,000 relocation bonus

  • $10,000 housing bonus

  • $1,500 per month meal stipend

  • Free Equinox membership

  • Monthly laundry reimbursement

  • Monthly personal wellness reimbursement

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance

  • 401(k) with company match

jobs.title: Research Intern
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Mercor

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.

 

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

About the Role

As a Research Scientist Intern at Mercor, you’ll work on research at the frontier of post-training, reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), data generation, and model evaluation.

You’ll investigate how datasets, rewards, and training methods affect the capabilities and behavior of large language models. This may include designing controlled experiments, developing new evaluation methodologies, conducting systematic failure analysis, and testing approaches to improve tool use, agentic behavior, and real-world reasoning.

You’ll work closely with research scientists, research engineers, and domain experts to turn open-ended questions into rigorous experiments. Your work will contribute to Mercor’s research agenda and may support external publications, benchmark releases, and the development of frontier AI systems.

What You’ll Do

  • Develop and investigate research questions related to post-training, RLVR, data quality, and model evaluation.

  • Design and run controlled experiments to understand how datasets, rewards, and training strategies affect model performance.

  • Study reward-shaping and post-training methods, including approaches such as GRPO and DAPO.

  • Develop methods for measuring data quality, usability, and performance uplift on key benchmarks.

  • Design and evaluate datasets, rubrics, evaluators, and scoring frameworks for complex model capabilities.

  • Conduct systematic error analysis to identify model failure modes and opportunities for improvement.

  • Analyze experimental results and communicate findings through clear reports, research artifacts, and presentations.

  • Build the research tooling and data pipelines needed to conduct experiments at scale.

  • Collaborate with research scientists, research engineers, applied AI teams, and domain experts producing training and evaluation data.

  • Contribute to research publications, benchmark releases, and other public research outputs where appropriate.

What We’re Looking For

  • Currently pursuing a master’s or PhD in computer science, machine learning, statistics, mathematics, or another relevant field.

  • Demonstrated ability to formulate research questions, design experiments, and draw sound conclusions from empirical results.

  • Demonstrated experience in at least one of the following:

    • Training, fine-tuning, or evaluating language models.

    • Agentic AI system, RL environments

    • Developing benchmarks, evaluation methodologies, or data-quality measures.

  • At least one publication or open source project.

  • Strong programming skills, particularly in Python, and the ability to write reliable research code.

  • Familiarity with machine learning fundamentals, experimental design, and statistical analysis.

  • Intellectual curiosity.

  • Comfort operating in a fast-paced research environment with rapid iteration and a high degree of ownership.

Nice to Have

  • Previous research experience in language models, reinforcement learning, model evaluation, or post-training.

  • Experience training, fine-tuning, or evaluating language models.

  • Familiarity with RLVR techniques, reward modeling, or agentic AI systems.

  • Experience developing benchmarks, evaluation methodologies, or data-quality measures.

  • Research publications or submissions at competitive CS conferences such as ACL, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, or EMNLP.

  • Research papers, technical reports, open-source projects, or other work samples demonstrating relevant skills.

Why Mercor

Impact: Your work powers how AI labs train and deploy their models

Learning: Get early exposure to frontier AI research and engineering

Growth: Work with a high-velocity team where interns ship to production

Benefits

  • Mentorship from experienced researchers.

  • Work on real, high-impact projects.

  • $1.5K monthly stipend for meals

  • $200 monthly laundry reimbursement

  • $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement

  • Free Equinox membership

  • Team events and offsites.

  • Potential full-time return offer.

We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

About the role:

We're looking for a Marketing Manager to run social, content, and campaigns across Mercor's marketing team.

Mercor is one of the fastest-growing companies in AI, and marketing runs with a small team and a big surface area: model launches, research, our podcast, events, customer campaigns, and the brand itself. You'll be hands-on across all of it, owning programs end to end from brief to launch to results.

This role suits someone early in their career who wants range and ownership. You'll work closely with product marketing, design, research, and GTM.

Key responsibilities:

  • Campaign execution: Plan and run integrated campaigns across email, social, web, and events, from the brief through launch and reporting.

  • Social: Run Mercor's presence on X and LinkedIn. Track what AI researchers, founders, and VCs are talking about. You are able to turn launches, research, and news into moments that take over the feed.

  • Podcast: Drive distribution for the podcast, including the launch plan and social clips for every episode.

  • Content: Write blog posts, emails, landing pages, and launch assets that meet a high quality bar.

  • Channels and web: Manage our owned channels and marketing site updates. Write and ship new landing pages and run experiments.

Must haves:

  • 2-4 years of marketing experience, ideally at a startup or high-growth company.

  • You live on X. You follow AI researchers, VC and tech enthusiasts on X and know what drives conversation.

  • You've run social for a brand or grown your own account.

  • You're an excellent writer and editor who can write for both technical and business audiences.

  • You have hands-on experience across more than one channel or area (content, email, social, events, web).

  • You use AI tools every day and have built at least one workflow or automation that saves time, but don’t rely on it for your writing.

  • You're scrappy and adaptable. You thrive in ambiguity, move fast, and are comfortable with changing priorities.

  • You're organized and detail-oriented. You can run several programs at once without dropping anything.

Bonus

  • Experience at an AI or developer-tools company

  • Experience editing short-form video or podcast clips

This role suits someone early in their career who wants range and ownership. You'll work closely with product marketing, design, research, and GTM.

Key responsibilities:

 - Campaign execution: Plan and run integrated campaigns across email, social, web, and events, from the brief through launch and reporting.

 - Social: Run Mercor's presence on X and LinkedIn. Track what AI researchers, founders, and VCs are talking about. You are able to turn launches, research, and news into moments that take over the feed.

 - Podcast: Drive distribution for the podcast, including the launch plan and social clips for every episode.

 - Content: Write blog posts, emails, landing pages, and launch assets that meet a high quality bar.

 - Channels and web: Manage our owned channels and marketing site updates. Write and ship new landing pages and run experiments.

Must haves:

 - 2-4 years of marketing experience, ideally at a startup or high-growth company.

 - You live on X. You follow AI researchers, VC and tech enthusiasts on X and know what drives conversation.

 - You've run social for a brand or grown your own account.

 - You're an excellent writer and editor who can write for both technical and business audiences.

 - You have hands-on experience across more than one channel or area (content, email, social, events, web).

 - You use AI tools every day and have built at least one workflow or automation that saves time, but don’t rely on it for your writing.

 - You're scrappy and adaptable. You thrive in ambiguity, move fast, and are comfortable with changing priorities.

 - You're organized and detail-oriented. You can run several programs at once without dropping anything.

Bonus

 - Experience at an AI or developer-tools company

 - Experience editing short-form video or podcast clips

  • Experience at a company that sells to or partners with AI labs

  • Background in AI infrastructure, data, or developer tools marketing

  • Familiarity with the AI benchmarking or evals landscape

jobs.title: People Programs Specialist
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Mercor

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.

 

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

The role

Mercor is growing at a pace few companies ever reach. We're bringing in new employees every week, many of our managers are leading teams for the first time, and the programs that support our people need to keep up.

We're looking for a People Programs Specialist who can make that happen.

You'll help run the programs that shape how employees join Mercor, how managers lead, how people develop and how we support employees throughout their time here. This is a role that combines program delivery, People operations, compliance and automation. You'll be just as comfortable facilitating a room of new managers as you are getting into an HR system, troubleshooting an onboarding issue or building a workflow that eliminates repetitive work.

You'll work directly with the Head of People and People Leads to shape priorities and improve programs, then take ownership of executing them. We want someone who can identify what needs to be done, bring ideas for making it better and follow through without needing constant direction.

There's plenty to build, and the scope will evolve as Mercor grows. You'll need to be comfortable working across different parts of People, learning quickly and taking on new challenges as they emerge.

What you'll do

Manager enablement and employee development

Many of Mercor's managers are leading people for the first time. You'll help give them the skills, tools and support to do it well.

  • Own the delivery of new manager onboarding and ongoing manager development programs, including scheduling, facilitation, communications and follow-up.

  • Facilitate training sessions on feedback, performance management, employee development and Mercor's management practices.

  • Partner with managers and People leadership to identify employee skill gaps and coordinate targeted upskilling opportunities.

  • Gather feedback from participants, track whether programs are working and make improvements to content and delivery.

  • Build repeatable training resources and tools that managers can use as their teams grow.

People programs and employee experience

You'll turn People priorities into programs that run reliably and produce measurable results.

  • Execute recurring People programs, including employee engagement surveys, feedback initiatives and development programs, from planning through delivery and reporting.

  • Coordinate communications, timelines and stakeholders so programs launch on time and employees understand what they need to do.

  • Track participation, adoption and outcomes, identify what isn't working and recommend changes.

  • Maintain clear, accessible employee resources, People policies and process documentation.

  • Help implement policies consistently, working with People leadership and relevant partners when questions or exceptions arise.

Employee lifecycle and onboarding

A strong employee experience starts with getting the operational details right. You'll help ensure employees can join, move within and leave Mercor through processes that are accurate, compliant and well coordinated.

  • Run end-to-end onboarding operations, from signed offer through an employee's first weeks, including background checks, I-9 verification, HRIS and payroll setup, benefits enrollment, equipment, systems access and orientation.

  • Coordinate closely with Talent, IT, Payroll and hiring managers to ensure employees are ready for their first day.

  • Facilitate onboarding sessions and continuously improve the new-hire experience.

  • Execute employee lifecycle changes, including role changes, team transfers, manager changes and offboarding, ensuring systems, documentation and relevant stakeholders stay aligned.

  • Coordinate immigration cases with outside counsel, tracking documentation, employee communications and deadlines.

  • Identify recurring onboarding and lifecycle issues and fix the processes behind them, rather than repeatedly solving the same problems.

People operations and compliance

Strong People programs depend on accurate systems, reliable processes and a solid understanding of employment requirements. Compliance isn't separate from employee experience. It's part of delivering it well.

  • Maintain accurate employee data, documentation and records across Mercor's People systems.

  • Own or support HRIS workflows and system administration for assigned People programs and lifecycle processes.

  • Ensure onboarding, employee changes and offboarding follow applicable compliance requirements, including I-9 verification and relevant multi-state employment obligations.

  • Track compliance deadlines and requirements within your scope, identify risks early and coordinate with Legal, Finance and other partners to resolve them.

  • Support internal and external audits by preparing records, validating data and addressing findings.

  • Assist with regulatory reporting, including EEO-1 and California pay data reporting, in partnership with People leadership, Legal and Finance.

Automation and continuous improvement

Mercor is an AI company. We expect our People team to use technology to work smarter, not just manage more manual processes as we grow.

  • Build and maintain automated workflows that reduce repetitive work, improve accuracy and make employee processes easier to navigate.

  • Use AI and no-code tools to create lightweight internal tools, improve communications and simplify People operations.

  • Identify opportunities to connect systems, improve handoffs and prevent errors before they affect employees.

  • Take ideas from problem identification through working solutions, testing them with users and improving them based on feedback.

  • Measure the impact of improvements, including time saved, errors reduced and better experiences for employees and managers.

What we're looking for

People programs and operational experience

  • 3+ years of hands-on experience in People programs, People operations or a similar role, ideally in a high-growth technology company.

  • Experience owning and executing People programs, not just contributing to them. You can explain what you built, what you personally managed and how you measured success.

  • Experience delivering employee training, manager enablement or learning programs, including facilitating sessions yourself.

  • Experience managing recurring programs and operational processes with multiple stakeholders, deadlines and dependencies.

Systems, compliance and automation

  • Working knowledge of the US employee lifecycle, including onboarding, I-9 requirements, multi-state considerations, employee changes and offboarding.

  • Hands-on experience administering HR systems, maintaining employee data and managing operational workflows.

  • Experience building automations or lightweight internal tools using AI, no-code or low-code platforms (such as Cursor, Retool or Zapier). We're looking for someone who has actually built things, not just identified opportunities to automate.

  • Experience maintaining compliance documentation, supporting audits or coordinating regulatory requirements.

  • Comfort working with Legal, Payroll, IT and outside providers to resolve operational issues.

How you work

  • You're confident facilitating groups, from welcoming a cohort of new hires to running a training session for managers.

  • You write clearly and practically. You can explain a policy, document a process and make complicated information easy for employees to understand.

  • You're detail-oriented and discreet with employee information, compliance requirements and time-sensitive processes.

  • You take ownership, anticipate problems and follow through without needing reminders.

  • You bring urgency without sacrificing accuracy, and you know when something needs to be escalated.

  • You're comfortable switching between running a program, solving an operational problem and building something new, even when the process isn't fully defined yet.

  • You look for ways to simplify and automate work rather than accepting repetitive manual processes.

Nice to haves

  • Experience enabling first-time managers in a rapidly scaling organization.

  • Experience with Rippling and employee service desk or ticketing tools.

  • Exposure to immigration coordination, international employees or employer-of-record arrangements.

  • Experience supporting EEO-1, California pay data reporting or other employment compliance reporting.

Why join Mercor

Build programs that matter. Your work will directly influence how managers lead, how employees develop and how people experience Mercor as we scale.

Work close to the decisions. You'll partner directly with the Head of People and collaborate with teams across the company. You'll have visibility into what the business needs and the opportunity to help shape how we respond.

Do more than maintain existing processes. There is real room to build, automate and improve how People operates. You'll be trusted to bring ideas, try solutions and own the results.

Grow with the company. As Mercor scales, the complexity and reach of our People programs will grow too. This is an opportunity to develop broad experience across People programs, operations, systems and employee development.

jobs.title: Chief of Staff, Product
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Mercor

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.

 

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

About the Role

As Chief of Staff to the Head of Product, you'll be the operational backbone of an org that helps the world's leading AI labs and enterprises transform human expertise into better AI models. Mercor is organizing humanity's expertise into better AI models for every lab and enterprise — and you'll make the team building it run.

You'll work directly with the Head of Product and leadership across every product area — Marketplace, Studio (annotation), RL Environments, and the Eval Platform — turning a fast-moving, multi-team org into a coherent, predictable machine. You'll balance long-term operating strategy with rapid execution, owning the cross-cutting work that falls between teams and directly shaping how well the product org performs. You'll also shape Mercor's customer-facing product narrative, driving deeper relationships across the AI ecosystem


What You'll Do

  • Run the operating rhythm: Establish and drive planning and review cadences across the product org, and prep leadership meetings end-to-end — agendas, pre-reads, the framing data, and follow-through on decisions.

  • Competitive intel

  • Hiring

  • Standardize roadmaps: Maintain a consistent format and quality bar across all product-area roadmaps so leadership can compare, sequence, and resource them apples-to-apples.

  • Own customer communication: Own the monthly product-offering update we send to customers: coordinate inputs from each area, edit to one voice, and ship it on schedule.

  • Build connective tissue: Stand up and coordinate the interfaces between Product and adjacent functions like product marketing and developer relations, so launches and roadmaps plug in cleanly.

  • Strengthen the team: Support product recruiting, own PM onboarding, and coordinate the performance-review process — keeping timelines, calibration, and the bar consistent.

  • Get in the weeds: Take on the highest-leverage cross-cutting initiatives that lack a natural owner, and run them to done.


What We're Looking For

  • Experience: 2+ years in a chief-of-staff, product-ops, strategy & ops, or PM role; exposure to fast-scaling teams preferred.

  • Product Intuition: You have a strong instinct for what a good product looks like and what's worth building, you can pressure-test a decision on the merits rather than procedurally.

  • High Ownership: You take full accountability for outcomes, not just outputs, and nothing drops on your watch.

  • Operational Excellence: You build lightweight processes that create clarity without adding bureaucracy.

  • Structured Communication: You write crisp, exec-ready docs and turn ambiguity into a clear plan others can run with.

  • Cross-Functional Influence: You get things done across teams without formal authority, earning trust from ICs and leadership alike.

  • Judgment & Discretion: You handle sensitive information and competing priorities with sound judgment and low ego.

  • Balance of Rigor & Vision: Equally comfortable running the numbers and framing the strategic narrative behind them.


Benefits

  • Bi-annual performance bonus structure

  • Generous equity grant vested over 4 years

  • Up to $15k Relocation bonus

  • $10K housing bonus (if you live within 0.5 miles of our office)

  • $1.5K monthly stipend for meals

  • Free Equinox membership

  • $200 monthly laundry reimbursement

  • $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement

  • Health, Dental, Vision insurance

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

The Role

Mercor produces all sorts of data of data types, for AI labs and enterprise customers. We're hiring someone to own pricing structures across our data types.

This person will build the pricing models, rate cards, and margin frameworks to ensure pricing is consistent and defensible.

What You'll Do

Acquisition pricing & cost modeling (buy side)

  • Establish fair market value for the data we buy — by data type, domain, and end buyer — and set the acquisition cost ceilings that bound what we'll pay

  • Track competitor bidding behavior and maintain the cost curves that tell us when to pay up to win a corpus and when to walk

  • Model fully-loaded cost to serve: acquisition price, extraction, human QC, anonymization/PII, and LLM inference — not just what we pay the vendor

  • Define the priceable unit for each data type — per repo, per file, per video minute, per audio hour — and the quality attributes that move price within a unit

Monetization & margin strategy (sell side)

  • Design pricing and packaging frameworks for data by data type, volume, format, and customer segment

  • Build rate cards and tiered pricing for recurring, repeatable data products

  • Own unit economics per deal and per data product, including transfer pricing, internal chargeback, and direct vs. indirect revenue attribution across account P&Ls

  • Build the pricing/forecasting toolkit Finance and leadership use to evaluate new data products before launch

  • Continuously test and refine pricing using win/loss data, renewal behavior, and market feedback

What We're Looking For

  • 6+ years in pricing strategy, monetization, revenue operations, or a related analytical/strategy role — ideally at a data, marketplace, or B2B SaaS company

  • Strong financial/quantitative modeling skills — fluent in Excel/Sheets; SQL a strong plus

  • Track record of building pricing models from scratch, not just tuning ones already in place

  • Comfortable operating with real ambiguity — public benchmarks for pricing data assets are thin, so structured judgment matters as much as data

  • Sharp cross-functional communicator — this person works daily with Sourcing, Sales, Finance, and Product

Nice to Have

  • Experience pricing a two-sided marketplace (a cost/supply side and a demand/sell side), not just a single-sided product

  • Background in AI training data, or market data

Benefits

  • Bi-annual performance bonus structure

  • Generous equity grant vested over 4 years

  • Up to $15k Relocation bonus

  • $10K proximity bonus (if you live within 0.5 miles of our office)

  • $1.5K monthly stipend for meals

  • Free Equinox membership

  • $200 monthly laundry reimbursement

  • $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement

  • Health, Dental, Vision insurance

jobs.title: Mercor AI Research Fund Grants: Economics of AI
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Mercor

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.

 

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

Mercor AI Research Fund Grants: Economics of AI

One of the biggest challenges facing the industry today is determining whether frontier AI is capable enough to deliver value in real-world settings. A model can perform well on benchmarks and still struggle in production. That’s why investing in research, realistic evaluations, and robust verification is critical.

Mercor is seeking to fund AI research on the economic impacts of AI. This is separate from the Mercor Research Fellowship, which funds individual experts (apply HERE), our $5m of safety funding awards (apply HERE), and our funding of benchmarking research.

The grant supports:

  • The time of experts from Mercor's platform

  • Researcher hours

  • API costs

  • Stipends for event and conference attendance

Budget Categories

Applications are grouped into three budget tiers. Please state your tier clearly in your application and ensure your overall budget ask falls within it:

  • Tier 1: under $50,000: Suited to focused, well-scoped projects such as pilot studies, evaluations, replications, or extensions of existing work. These applications undergo a streamlined review.

  • Tier 2: under $200,000: Suited to substantial projects requiring dedicated personnel time, meaningful compute, or data collection. Reviewed with proportionally greater attention to the budget breakdown and implementation plan.

  • Tier 3: under $500,000: Reserved for ambitious, multi-component research programs. These applications receive the highest level of scrutiny: reviewers will expect a detailed justification of each spend category, a clear account of team capacity to execute at this scale, and milestones against which progress can be assessed.

The level of review scrutiny scales with the size of the ask, so applicants should request the smallest budget that credibly supports the proposed work.

 

Research Agenda

 

We are interested in submissions in the following area:

1. Measuring AI’s impact on labor

  • How should we measure AI’s effect on real economic and labor outcomes — and what methodologies are up to the task?

  • To what extent do benchmark scores map onto real economic outcomes?

  • What is the right methodology for measuring AI’s impact on labor outcomes (employment, wages, task composition)?

  • How does occupational exposure to AI evolve over time, and how can novel datasets improve its measurement?

2. Human–AI collaboration and productivity

  • How do humans actually work with AI systems, and when does that collaboration make them more productive?

  • What is the efficiency gain of human experts when paired with AI models, and under what conditions?

  • How can we measure the “review cost” that model outputs impose on humans — the time and effort spent checking, correcting, and verifying AI work?

  • Which collaboration patterns improve output quality rather than merely output volume?

3. Enterprise adoption and returns

  • What does AI adoption look like inside organizations, and what returns does it generate?

  • How are organizations actually using AI, and how is that usage changing?

  • How can the effect of AI and agent deployments be measured causally, rather than through self-report or correlation?

  • What are the right enterprise-level variables for quantifying AI-driven productivity gains?

 

Eligibility

 

  • Researchers at universities and non-profit research organizations, as well as public benefit corporations and small startups (<20 people) that do not sell AI training data. Awards are made to the researcher’s institution.

  • Applicants must be based in the United States or the United Kingdom

We expect grantees to publish a paper, an open dataset, a public methodology, or a tool the field can use, released under an open license that permits commercial use.

 

Timeline

 

  • Application deadline: November 27, 2026, 11:59 PM PT (UTC−8)

  • Notification to applicants: by December 18, 2026

Late or incomplete applications will not be reviewed. All applicants will be notified of the outcome whether or not they are shortlisted.

 
 

How to apply

We invite interested researchers to submit a brief Expression of Interest (EOI) before preparing a full proposal. The EOI should be ~1–3 pages and include:

  • Research question and background (max 250 words): What are you trying to do? State your objective in plain language, with minimal jargon. How is this problem addressed today, and what are the limits of current practice? Who cares: if you succeed, what difference will it make, and to whom?

  • Project proposal (max 400 words): Concrete technical and implementation detail: your approach, methods, datasets, models, compute, and evaluation plan.

  • Novelty (max 200 words): What is new in your approach relative to existing and ongoing work, and why do you believe it will succeed where current practice falls short?

  • Risks (max 150 words): What are the main technical and execution risks, and how will you mitigate or detect them early?

  • Team (max 100 words; if the team is large, up to 200): The researchers on the project and their relevant background and prior work.

  • Proposed outcomes and timeline: Expected deliverables (papers, artifacts, datasets, tools) and key milestones, including how long the work will take. Include the mid-term and final “exams”: the checkpoints and success criteria by which we will know whether the project is on track and succeeds.

  • Budget overview: How much will it cost? Provide a specific overall budget ask, your budget tier (see Budget Categories), and a breakdown by spend category (e.g., personnel, compute, data, travel/other).

    • Other sources of funding for this project should be clearly identified in the proposal budget

Guidance for applicants.

  • Strong EOIs are specific rather than high-level: they name the methods, systems, and evaluation criteria they will use, and they engage directly with existing literature and ongoing efforts rather than describing the problem space in general terms.

  • The EOI should briefly establish the PI’s (and key team members’) relevant background and prior work; proposals without demonstrated expertise in the research area are rarely competitive. Researchers with experience with agentic evaluation, RL environments, and post-training are encouraged to apply

  • Proposals that duplicate work already being pursued by many other groups are unlikely to advance unless they offer a clearly differentiated angle.

  • Please do not include confidential or proprietary information in your Expression of Interest. Submitting an Expression of Interest does not obligate Mercor to make an award.

 
 

Award terms

Selected grantees will sign Mercor’s research award agreement. Key terms include:

  • Grantees keep ownership of their work and grant Mercor a non-exclusive license to use it, including commercially.

  • Mercor may identify grantees and their institutions as award recipients, including by name and logo. Grantees may use Mercor’s logo with Mercor’s approval.

  • For benchmark and evaluation projects, Mercor receives early access to the benchmark before public release and the exclusive right to build and host a private held-out test set, at Mercor’s cost.

  • Grantees are free to publish their findings. Mercor reviews drafts in advance only to remove its confidential information.

  • Awards are subject to tax documentation, sanctions screening, and periodic progress reports.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Mercor

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

About the Role

Mercor is seeking a high-execution payroll leader to spearhead global payroll delivery while scaling our underlying operational infrastructure. In this role, you will hold end-to-end accountability for payroll execution schedules, vendor governance, internal controls, general ledger reconciliations, and complex issue resolution, all while driving high-impact automation initiatives. Additionally, you will orchestrate the seamless transition of acquired talent onto Mercor's unified payroll architecture.

Working cross-functionally, you will collaborate closely with Accounting, People Ops, Finance Systems, Legal, and international payroll partners. This position demands a mix of strategic oversight and hands-on execution—diving deep into operational mechanics, driving swift decision-making within structured framework guidelines, and proactively flagging operational bottlenecks to executive leadership.

What You'll Do

  • Run employee payroll cycles across assigned countries, coordinating inputs, validations, approvals, funding deadlines, and provider processing so employees are paid accurately and on time.

  • Review new hires, departures, compensation changes, bonuses, benefits, deductions, and equity-related payroll inputs with functional owners; investigate exceptions before approval.

  • Reconcile payroll outputs to approved inputs, funding, and accounting records. Partner with Accounting on journals, accruals, balance sheet reconciliations, and month-end close.

  • Maintain country calendars and evidence of required filings and remittances, working with providers and local advisers to resolve issues and complete year-end activities.

  • Lead payroll workstreams for acquisitions and new-country launches, including data mapping, cutover planning, testing, parallel runs where appropriate, and post-launch reconciliation.

  • Improve HRIS-to-payroll data flows, approval workflows, and reporting. Deliver scoped implementations and vendor transitions with documented requirements and acceptance criteria.

  • Build operating procedures, backup coverage, access controls, and audit evidence, maintaining separate preparation and approval responsibilities for payroll and payments.

  • Resolve employee pay questions clearly and promptly. Track accuracy, on-time delivery, reconciliation aging, and issue resolution, and address recurring causes.

  • Automate repeatable checks and reporting using approved tools, with validation, human review, and appropriate protection of employee data.

What We're Looking For

  • 7+ years of progressive payroll experience in high-growth tech startups

  • Hands-on ownership of US payroll and experience delivering payroll in additional countries through local teams or providers.

  • Strong understanding of payroll processing, reconciliations, statutory deadlines, controls, and year-end reporting, with judgment about when to involve local tax or legal specialists.

  • Experience delivering a payroll optimization, vendor transition, acquisition integration, or new-country launch from planning through stabilization.

  • Practical experience with an enterprise HRIS and payroll platform, including data validation, reporting, testing, and troubleshooting. Rippling or comparable systems experience is valuable.

  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage competing deadlines and influence partners without direct authority.

  • Clear communication, sound judgment with confidential information, and willingness to stay close to operational work.

  • A degree in Accounting, Finance, HR, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.


Nice to Have

  • EMEA or APAC payroll

  • Equity or mobility payroll

  • Hourly payroll and timekeeping

  • CPP or comparable certification


Compensation

  • Base cash comp from $160K - $185k

  • Generous equity grant vested over 4 years

  • Up to $15k Relocation bonus

  • $10K housing bonus (if you live within 0.5 miles of our office)

  • $1.5K monthly stipend for meals

  • Free Equinox membership

  • $200 monthly laundry reimbursement

  • $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement

  • Health, Dental, Vision insurance

  • 401(k) with company match

Mercor expands via strategic acquisitions, where critical financial risks surface within due diligence findings, transaction structures, and post-closing operational timelines. As Strategic Transactions Lead, you will spearhead the accounting workstream across every transaction, managing processes from post-LOI confirmatory diligence through the initial post-close annual audit.

Serving as the Controller team's representative on deal execution pods, you will partner closely with Corporate Finance, Legal, Business Operations, and Integration leads to ensure seamless financial consolidation. This key foundational role requires an operational builder who will construct robust diligence frameworks, establish key performance metrics, and scale M&A infrastructure alongside rapid acquisition velocity.

What You'll Do


Confirmatory Diligence

  • Direct post-LOI accounting due diligence, evaluating historical quality of earnings, revenue recognition policies, cap table structures, tax liabilities, and vendor obligations.

  • Construct scalable diligence playbooks tailored across diverse transaction types, including acquihires, IP assets, and complex business combinations.

  • Deliver comprehensive accounting readiness evaluations prior to execution, highlighting material risks and structuring implications.

  • Analyze definitive transaction documentation and settlement flows, advising leadership on earnouts, working capital adjustments, escrow holdbacks, and equity rollovers.

Deal Accounting

  • Oversee third-party valuation specialists on purchase price allocations, intangible asset valuations, and contingent consideration models.

  • Evaluate financial statement impacts for proposed deal mechanics and talent retention structures to guide executive decision-making.

  • Coordinate Day 1 close readiness across financial systems, payroll platforms, banking structures, and internal governance controls.

Post-Merger Integration

  • Lead the end-to-end accounting integration roadmap, including opening balance sheets, general ledger mappings, ERP migrations, policy alignment, and intercompany settlements.

  • Translate purchase terms into actionable operational milestones, aligning dependencies closely with the broader Corporate Development integration team.

  • Manage concurrent integration tracks across multiple acquired entities, maintaining delivery timelines and resolving operational blockers.

  • Transition acquired business units into Mercor's internal control environment and SOX-compliant reporting frameworks.

  • Serve as the main financial liaison for target leadership teams throughout the post-acquisition transition period.

Program Governance

  • Manage measurement-period adjustments, earnout tracking, intangible asset amortization schedules, and annual goodwill impairment testing.

  • Represent Mercor as the lead contact for external audit partners regarding complex M&A transactions.

  • Develop standardized M&A accounting toolkits, standardized templates, and cross-functional decision trees.

  • Conduct deal retrospectives while tracking performance metrics like close-cycle duration and post-close audit adjustments.

  • Mentor junior team members and review technical deliverables to build team capability.

What We're Looking For

  • 6+ years of combined experience across technical accounting, Big 4 audit, or transaction advisory services

  • 2+ years of in-house financeops experience within high-growth, venture-backed technology environments

  • Proven track record leading M&A accounting end-to-end across multiple closed acquisitions

  • Deep expertise in US GAAP technical frameworks, including ASC 805, ASC 606, ASC 718, and ASC 820

  • Strong operational execution skills, you convert transaction terms into clear, actionable integration workstreams

  • Exceptional communication skills, ability to translate technical accounting positions to cross-functional executives, legal counsel, and auditors

  • Active Certified Public Accountant (CPA) license


Nice to Have

  • Direct experience accounting for acquihires, including retention vs. consideration evaluation

  • Background in Big 4 financial due diligence (FDD) or deal advisory practices

  • Experience establishing an M&A accounting practice, playbooks, and governance frameworks from scratch

  • Demonstrated capability managing multiple concurrent transaction integrations under tight timelines

  • Familiarity with cross-border acquisition structures and foreign subsidiary integration

  • Experience working in fast-paced AI or hyper-growth technology environments


Compensation

  • Base cash comp from $175K - $210k

  • Generous equity grant vested over 4 years

  • Up to $15k Relocation bonus

  • $10K housing bonus (if you live within 0.5 miles of our office)

  • $1.5K monthly stipend for meals

  • Free Equinox membership

  • $200 monthly laundry reimbursement

  • $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement

  • Health, Dental, Vision insurance

  • 401(k) with company match

jobs.title: AI Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Mercor

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.

 

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

Summary of role:

All of Mercor’s AI work, from training and serving models to building agents, runs on GPUs. Your job is to make that compute fast, fault-tolerant and fully utilized.

You’ll own the accelerator platform end to end. That means the clusters and schedulers across AWS, GCP, neoclouds and on-prem, the training and LLM serving on top, and the observability and cost data that show where every GPU-hour goes.

This is a software engineering role, not an ops role. You’ll write production code every day, own systems from design through on-call, and build the platform that sets how fast Mercor can move.

Representative projects

  • Stand up a multi-cloud GPU fleet spanning hyperscalers, neoclouds and on-prem, orchestrated through custom Kubernetes and Slurm operators so researchers never have to think about where their job lands.

  • Build a scheduling layer with gang scheduling, bin-packing and fair-share quotas that measurably raises accelerator utilization across teams.

  • Ship a high-throughput vLLM serving stack with prefill/decode disaggregation, KV cache offload and FP8/FP4 quantization. Back it with a benchmarking and traffic-replay harness that tracks TTFT, TPOT and latency percentiles against per-config baselines.

  • Build a self-healing health-check and remediation system that rides out fault storms across hardware, network and software without paging a human.

  • Build an end-to-end cost-attribution pipeline. It ingests utilization, occupancy and billing data into the warehouse, attributes every GPU-hour to a team and workload, and drives capacity planning.

  • Build internal tools and dashboards that researchers and non-engineers use every day.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Design, deploy and operate GPU clusters across AWS, GCP, and other hyperscalers/neoclouds/on-premise data centers, including custom Kubernetes and Slurm operators and the metadata services behind them.

  • Build scheduling that keeps accelerators busy: gang scheduling for distributed jobs, bin-packing to reduce fragmentation, and quotas and fair share for multi-tenant teams.

  • Run distributed training infrastructure on PyTorch Distributed, Ray, or Megatron, with fast checkpointing and model loading.

  • Deploy and tune high-throughput LLM serving with vLLM or similar: tensor and model/expert parallelism, prefill/decode disaggregation, KV cache offload, FP8/FP4 quantization.

  • Build benchmarking and traffic-replay tools that measure TTFT, TPOT and latency percentiles, and set per-config performance baselines.

  • Build health checks across hardware, network and software layers, and automated remediation that handles fault storms without human intervention.

  • Instrument fleet utilization with DCGM, Prometheus and Grafana. Write recording rules and alerts that teams rely on.

  • Ingest utilization, occupancy and billing data into a warehouse, attribute spend to teams and workloads, and support capacity planning.

  • Drive autoscaling, rightsizing and idle-capacity recovery programs with measurable cost results.

  • Write clear runbooks and documentation, and explain infrastructure tradeoffs to researchers, finance and leadership.

  • Build internal tools or dashboards that researchers and non-engineers use daily.

You may be a good fit if you

  • Have 5+ years building and operating production distributed systems or ML infrastructure

  • Write production-quality Python plus Go or C++, and are fluent in shell scripting for system administration.

  • Have deep hands-on Kubernetes and container experience, plus working knowledge of Slurm or another HPC resource manager.

  • Have run GPU workloads at scale, including scheduling, orchestration and troubleshooting.

  • Have hands-on experience with at least one distributed training or serving stack: PyTorch Distributed, Ray, vLLM or Megatron-LM.

  • Have deep experience with at least one major cloud provider.

  • Know observability tools like DataDog, Prometheus, PromQL and Grafana, and are comfortable on-call for critical systems.

  • Own projects end to end and gather your own requirements with little direction.

Strong candidates may also have experience with (or a strong desire to learn deeply)

  • LLM inference optimization: KV cache systems, disaggregated serving, quantization, speculative decoding

  • High-performance networking: RDMA, InfiniBand, NCCL, NVLink

  • GPU profiling with Nsight or similar, and CUDA or Triton kernel work

  • Accelerators beyond NVIDIA: AMD MI-series, TPU, Trainium

  • Capacity planning, billing normalization or cost attribution across providers

  • Automated fault diagnosis, log mining or AIOps at fleet scale

  • Configuration management (Ansible, Puppet) and secure or air-gapped deployments

Benefits

  • Bi-annual performance bonus structure

  • Generous equity grant vested over 4 years

  • Up to $15k Relocation bonus

  • $10K housing bonus (if you live within 0.5 miles of our office)

  • $1.5K monthly stipend for meals

  • Free Equinox membership

  • $200 monthly laundry reimbursement

  • $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement

  • Health, Dental, Vision insurance

About the Role

As a Technical Recruiter at Mercor, you’ll own full-cycle hiring across critical technical functions, partnering directly with the VP of Engineering, CTO, and engineering leadership. You’ll play a foundational role in shaping our engineering organization as we scale one of the fastest-growing companies in the world.

What You’ll Do

  • Own full-cycle recruiting across software, machine learning, research, infrastructure, security, and leadership roles.

  • Partner directly with the VP of Engineering, CTO, and Engineering Managers to define headcount plans, role outcomes, success profiles, and the hiring bar. Prioritize reqs against business goals.

  • Build top-of-funnel through targeted passive outreach, talent intelligence, referrals, events, and Mercor’s own product (structured screens, automated work samples, and calibrated rubrics).

  • Source and close passive, high-bar candidates. Lead with a compelling narrative, handle objections, and drive offer strategy and negotiations aligned to leveling, comp bands, and market data.

  • Design assessments that predict on-the-job performance. Define competencies, calibrate rubrics, and keep raising signal quality.

  • Coach hiring managers and interviewers on structured interviewing, leveling, and decision hygiene.

  • Operationalize hiring systems. Track and optimize pass-through rates, time-in-stage, source yield, and diversity signals, and report weekly and quarterly with clear metrics and narrative.

  • Champion speed and quality: drive SLAs for same-day debriefs and fast offers, and maintain a consistently strong candidate experience.

  • Maintain a mapped bench of high-potential talent for critical and future roles.

  • Build Mercor’s brand with top technical talent through campaigns, content, communities, and events. You’ll be a face of Mercor for the engineers and researchers we want most.

  • Partner on dashboards, metrics, and process automation in Ashby and other recruiting systems.

What We're Looking For

  • 6+ years of full-cycle technical recruiting, ideally in high-growth or deep-tech environments.

  • Deep familiarity with technical roles: SWE, MLE, Research, Applied AI, Security, Infrastructure, and TLM.

  • A proven track record of sourcing and closing passive candidates for high-bar IC and leadership roles.

  • Demonstrated ability to build and scale hiring systems, identify the right metrics, and make data-driven decisions.

  • Fluency with structured interviewing, competency rubrics, and recruiting analytics.

  • Strong communication skills and the ability to influence senior stakeholders, including the VP of Engineering, the CTO, and cross-functional leaders, at pace.

  • Commitment to inclusive hiring and an excellent candidate experience.

  • Familiarity with Ashby, or the ability to pick up new tools quickly.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience as a founding technical recruiter or early-stage builder.

  • Experience hiring ML researchers or research engineers at an AI lab.

  • Interest in the human data / AGI space.

  • A technical degree or professional engineering experience.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Bi-annual performance bonus structure

  • Generous equity grant vested over 4 years

  • Up to $15k Relocation bonus

  • $10K housing bonus (if you live within 0.5 miles of our office)

  • $1.5K monthly stipend for meals

  • $200 monthly laundry reimbursement

  • $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement

  • Health, Dental, Vision insurance

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Mercor

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

About the role

We are seeking a Procurement Ops Specialist to support Mercor’s procurement operations, vendor onboarding, and employee purchasing experience. You will manage helpdesk requests and procurement intake, coordinate contract signatures and purchase orders, and partner with Accounts Payable to unblock aged invoices. You will also support user training & procurement systems testing.

What You'll Do

 

  • Purchasing operations. Validate pricing, legal entities, categories, and requisition lines; create and finalize purchase orders and change orders in the procurement platform.

  • Vendor onboarding. Follow up with vendors for missing information, review tax and banking documentation for completeness under company procedures, and maintain accurate vendor profiles.

  • Aged invoice resolution. Support Accounts Payable in unblocking aged invoices by following up with business requesters to obtain or resolve missing purchase orders and coordinating outstanding actions.

  • Contract signatures. Route contracts for signature in Ironclad, coordinate with internal stakeholders and vendors, and track signatures through completion.

  • Procurement helpdesk. Triage requests; assess urgency, route questions to the right owners, and track issues through resolution.

  • Intake and service levels. Monitor procurement intake and follow up with cross-functional stakeholders to meet established service-level agreements and keep requests moving.

  • Training and systems support. Train users on procurement workflows and supporting tools

 

What we’re looking for

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in procurement operations or procure-to-pay support, including requisitions, purchase orders, and change orders.

  • Experience supporting vendor onboarding, vendor data, contract coordination, and employee helpdesk requests.

  • Deep familiarity with procurement/P2P tooling (e.g. Ramp, Ironclad, Zip, or similar) and a bias toward automation over manual work.

  • Strong attention to detail when reviewing pricing, entities, categories, and purchasing records; discretion with sensitive vendor and banking information.

  • Working knowledge of AP and payment processes, so you can hand off cleanly to AP and troubleshoot upstream issues before they become AP's problem.

  • Clear communication and strong organization, with the ability to manage deadlines, coordinate cross-functional follow-ups, and train users.

What You’ll Do

  • Drive your own roadmap: Partner directly with stakeholders, proactively identify high-impact problems, and independently prioritize and execute solutions.

  • Own analytics end-to-end: Translate ambiguous business problems into production-ready data models, dashboards, and analytical tools.

  • Automate business workflows: Identify operational bottlenecks and build automations that eliminate manual work and improve efficiency.

  • Leverage AI to multiply output: Use AI coding agents and emerging tools to accelerate development and continuously improve how analytics engineering gets done.


What We’re Looking For

  • 8+ years of experience in Analytics Engineering, Data Engineering, Data Science, or a related technical role.

  • Strong technical fundamentals: Expert SQL, data modeling, Python, dbt, cloud data warehouses, and BI tools (e.g., Hex, Looker).

  • Exceptional autonomy: Proven ability to independently identify problems, define roadmaps, and deliver high-impact projects with minimal direction.

  • Strong business judgment and communication: Able to work directly with senior stakeholders, understand business priorities, and translate ambiguity into actionable solutions.

Mercor operates at an exceptionally fast pace. This role is based in our San Francisco office five days per week, and our teams commonly work 9 AM–9 PM. We’re looking for people who are energized by this level of commitment, autonomy, and execution.

jobs.title: Research Engineer Intern - Environments, Data and Post-Training
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Mercor

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.

 

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

About the Role

As a Research Engineer at Mercor, you’ll work at the intersection of engineering and applied AI research. You’ll contribute directly to post-training and RLVR, synthetic data generation, and large-scale evaluation workflows that meaningfully impact frontier language models.

Your work will be used to train large language models to master tool use, agentic behavior, and real-world reasoning in real-world production environments. You’ll shape rewards, run post-training experiments, and build scalable systems that improve model performance. You’ll help design and evaluate datasets, create scalable data augmentation pipelines, and build rubrics and evaluators that push the boundaries of what LLMs can learn.

What You’ll Do

  • Work on post-training and RLVR pipelines to understand how datasets, rewards, and training strategies impact model performance.

  • Design and run reward-shaping experiments and algorithmic improvements (e.g., GRPO, DAPO) to improve LLM tool-use, agentic behavior, and real-world reasoning.

  • Quantify data usability, quality, and performance uplift on key benchmarks.

  • Build and maintain data generation and augmentation pipelines that scale with training needs.

  • Create and refine rubrics, evaluators, and scoring frameworks that guide training and evaluation decisions.

  • Build and operate LLM evaluation systems, benchmarks, and metrics at scale.

  • Collaborate closely with AI researchers, applied AI teams, and experts producing training data.

  • Operate in a fast-paced, experimental research environment with rapid iteration cycles and high ownership.

What We’re Looking For

  • Strong applied research background, with a focus on post-training and/or model evaluation.

  • Strong coding proficiency and hands-on experience working with machine learning models.

  • Strong understanding of data structures, algorithms, backend systems, and core engineering fundamentals.

  • Familiarity with APIs, SQL/NoSQL databases, and cloud platforms.

  • Ability to reason deeply about model behavior, experimental results, and data quality.

  • Excitement to work in person in San Francisco, five days a week (with optional remote Saturdays), and thrive in a high-intensity, high-ownership environment.

Nice To Have

  • Real-world post-training team experience in industry (highest priority).

  • Publications at top-tier conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ACL).

  • Experience training models or evaluating model performance.

  • Experience in synthetic data generation, LLM evaluations, or RL-style workflows.

  • Work samples, artifacts, or code repositories demonstrating relevant skills.

Benefits

  • Health Benefits eligible at 30+ hours a week

  • Overtime eligible at 1.5x from 40 to 55 hours; 2x over 55 hours-week.

  • $1.5K monthly stipend for meals

  • Relocation & Housing Support

  • Free Equinox membership

  • $200 monthly laundry reimbursement

  • $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement

jobs.title: Research Engineer, Intern – Benchmarking
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Mercor

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.

 

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

About the Role

As a Research Engineer at Mercor, you’ll work at the intersection of engineering and applied AI research. You’ll own benchmarking pipelines, evaluation systems, and failure analysis workflows that directly inform how we train and improve frontier language models.
Your work will define how we measure tool use, agentic behavior, and real-world reasoning. You’ll design and run evals, build rubrics and scorers, and turn failure analysis into actionable improvements for post-training, RLVR, and data pipelines.

What You’ll Do

  • Benchmarking: Design, implement, and maintain benchmarks and metrics for tool use, agentic behavior, and real-world reasoning; ensure benchmarks scale with training and stay aligned with product and research goals.

  • Evaluation systems: Build and operate LLM evaluation systems end-to-end runs, scoring, dashboards, and reporting, so researchers and applied AI teams can track model performance and compare runs at scale.

  • Failure analysis: Run systematic failure analysis on model outputs (e.g., wrong tool use, reasoning errors, safety/alignment issues); categorize failure modes, quantify prevalence, and feed findings into reward design, data curation, and benchmark design.

  • Rubrics and evaluators: Create and refine rubrics, automated evaluators, and scoring frameworks that drive training and evaluation decisions; balance rigor with scalability (human vs. model-as-judge, calibration, agreement).

  • Data quality and usability: Quantify data usability, quality, and impact on key benchmarks; use evals and failure analysis to guide data generation, augmentation, and curation.

  • Cross-team collaboration: Work with AI researchers, applied AI teams, and data producers to align evals with training objectives and to prioritize benchmarks and failure analyses that matter most.

  • Ownership in a fast-paced environment: Operate in a high-iteration research setting with strong ownership of benchmarks, evals, and failure-analysis workflows.

What We’re Looking For

  • Strong applied research background, with focus on model evaluation, benchmarking, and/or failure analysis.

  • Strong coding skills and hands-on experience with ML models and evaluation code.

  • Solid grasp of data structures, algorithms, and backend systems.

  • Comfort with APIs, SQL/NoSQL, and cloud platforms for running and storing eval results.

  • Ability to reason about model behavior, experimental results, and data quality from evals and failure analyses.

  • Excitement to work in person in San Francisco five days a week in a high-intensity, high-ownership environment.

Nice To Have

  • Industry experience on a post-training or evaluation/benchmarking team (highest priority).

  • Publications at top-tier venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ACL), especially in evaluation or benchmarking.

  • Experience building or running LLM evaluations, benchmarks, or failure-analysis pipelines.

  • Experience with synthetic data generation, rubric design, or RL-style workflows that use evals for reward shaping.

  • Work samples or code (e.g., eval frameworks, benchmark suites, failure-analysis reports or tooling) that demonstrate relevant skills.

Benefits

  • Health Benefits eligible at 30+ hours a week

  • Overtime eligible at 1.5x from 40 to 55 hours; 2x over 55 hours-week.

  • $1.5K monthly stipend for meals

  • Relocation & Housing Support

  • Free Equinox membership

  • $200 monthly laundry reimbursement

  • $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement

What You’ll Do

  • Own full-cycle recruiting (sourcing → close) across a variety of organizations such as marketing, finance, legal and people ops

  • Partner directly with C-Suite Leadership to map out needs and implement continual process improvements

  • Coach hiring managers and interviewers on structured interviewing, leveling, and decision hygiene

  • Operationalize hiring systems: track and optimize key funnel metrics (pass-through rates, time-in-stage, source yield)

  • Champion speed and quality: drive SLAs for same-day debriefs, fast offers, and strong candidate experience

  • Build brand: campaigns, referrals, and events that attract top engineers and operators

  • Represent Mercor externally, you’ll be a face of the brand for an exceptionally competitive talent market

  • Collaborate on dashboards, metrics, and process automation within Ashby and other recruiting systems

What We’re Looking For

  • Proven success hiring across a range of roles and departments, with the ability to context switch across departments with ease

  • Ability to build and scale hiring systems, identify key metrics, and make data-driven decisions

  • Strong communication skills; able to work efficiently with General Managers, Strategic Project Leads and Mercor’s President

  • Confident representing the Mercor brand to top candidates

  • Familiarity with Ashby or ability to quickly adopt new tools and systems

     

Nice to Haves

  • Commitment to the Outcome - Ownership mentality; will hold themselves accountable to an extremely high standard of work

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own full-cycle recruiting (sourcing → close) across a variety of organizations such as marketing, finance, legal and people ops

 - Partner directly with C-Suite Leadership to map out needs and implement continual process improvements

 - Build top-of-funnel using creative outbound, talent intelligence, and Mercor’s own product (structured screens, automated work samples, and calibrated rubrics)

 - Coach hiring managers and interviewers on structured interviewing, leveling, and decision hygiene

 - Operationalize hiring systems: track and optimize key funnel metrics (pass-through rates, time-in-stage, source yield)

 - Champion speed and quality: drive SLAs for same-day debriefs, fast offers, and strong candidate experience

 - Build brand: campaigns, referrals, and events that attract top engineers and operators

 - Represent Mercor externally, you’ll be a face of the brand for an exceptionally competitive talent market

 - Collaborate on dashboards, metrics, and process automation within Ashby and other recruiting systems

 - Refinement of technical recruiting motion as the Ops org shifts to hire more frequently from technical backgrounds
   
    


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 5+ years experience with full-cycle recruiting across IC and leadership roles

 - Proven success hiring across a range of roles and departments, with the ability to context switch across departments with ease

 - Ability to build and scale hiring systems, identify key metrics, and make data-driven decisions

 - Strong communication skills; able to work efficiently with General Managers, Strategic Project Leads and Mercor’s President

 - Confident representing the Mercor brand to top candidates

 - Familiarity with Ashby or ability to quickly adopt new tools and systems
   
    


NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience as a founding recruiter or early-stage startup builder

 - Interest in the human data / AGI space

 - Prior experience leveraging Ashby as an ATS
   
    


IDEAL QUALITIES

 - Agility / Adaptability - ability to move fast, pivot with business shifts, and maintain best-in-class outcomes

 - Operational Rigor - ability to bring order to an unstructured environment

 - Growth Mindset - You don’t need to be an expert on AI, but you do need to have a strong desire to learn and continue learning in a rapidly evolving, frontier industry

 - Commitment to the Outcome - Ownership mentality; will hold themselves accountable to an extremely high standard of work
